Gambits — Gambit abilities either work to great effect or have a negative consequence on failure.
Disarm — The Duelist specializes in rare and powerful disarm techniques. She can disarm opponents and take advantage after the target is disarmed.
Allied Coordination — For each ally that is ready at the same time the Phalanx uses her abilities, the more powerful they are. Some abilities require multiple allies to be ready simultaneously.

Succession — Succession abilities are dual-wield attacks whose second hit gains enhanced effects based on dual-wield attack speed. The faster her attacks land, the more powerful the succession payoff.

Bushido — Some Samurai abilities allow enemies to attack her first, though many also delay or reset the enemy's counter afterward. These abilities are stronger relative to the effect of the enemy's action, encouraging the Samurai to fight her most difficult foe.
Feints — Feint abilities can come in any action type and all compel an enemy and improve the Swashbuckler's parry chance. They grant a reaction on parrying and require a level of expertise.
Unstoppable Abilities — Dreadnaughts can use their defense to augment physical attacks, enhancing damage or causing other effects.

Scavenged Abilities — Scavenged abilities are prepared. On preparation, one of the six primary elements (air, earth, fire, water, light, dark) is randomly selected and locked in. The chosen element is displayed publicly and cannot be changed without consuming or disrupting the ability. This makes scavenged abilities less flexible than standard abilities but potentially more powerful, as the element is committed before targeting decisions are made.

Premade Concoctions — Premade abilities begin each wave already prepared at no resource or action cost. The first use requires no ammo and the prepared state cannot be disrupted in the conventional sense — only breaking the vial through combat disruption prevents it. After the first use, premade abilities must be re-prepared using the standard preparation system with a mana cost and can be disrupted during preparation. Premades are slightly less powerful than equivalent standard abilities in exchange for their zero-cost first use.

Accumulation — Accumulation abilities have two uses. The first use activates the ability and begins accumulating power; the ability grows stronger with each clock tick it remains active. The second use expends all accumulated power in a single discharge. The three Accumulator abilities (Beam, Burst, Storm) consume all active ammo on first use — the amount consumed and the active ammo type at that moment determine the base power and damage type when fired. Accumulating Detonation and Accumulating Trap accumulate power over time with no ammo cost.

Modifications — Modifications are toggled abilities that alter how the Tinker and her companions function. Each modification costs a move action to toggle on and a move action to toggle off. Any number of modifications can be active simultaneously. Some modifications affect only the Tinker’s abilities, some affect only the companion, and some affect both. Four major abilities — Modular Bomb, Modular Ray, Modular Trap, and Modular Beam — each function differently depending on which modifications are currently active.

Assistants — Assistant abilities are move-action enchantments placed on chosen allies. Each assistant type grants a different proc that fires whenever the assigned ally attacks. Multiple different assistant types can be active simultaneously on different allies. Each assistant type can only be assigned to one ally at a time — reassigning it to a new ally removes it from the previous one. Assistants that use ammo consume one ammo each time their proc fires. Assistants persist on the ally until reassigned.

Friendly Fire — The Bomber’s bomb abilities deal high area damage but apply the same damage to allies as to enemies. Base damage values are identical for all targets — there is no ally discount. Scaling abilities scale the same way for all targets.

Called Shots — Called shot abilities are prepared as a minor action. Each called shot names a specific target at preparation time and applies a powerful secondary effect to the first attack ability used against that target on the following turn. Without the capstone skill Quick Call, the called shot cannot be used and applied on the same turn — the minor action prepares the effect and the attack comes next turn.

Concoction Detonations — The Savant’s six concoction abilities are detonations with three phases. While placed on a target they apply an ongoing effect. Simultaneously, they accumulate power each clock tick from the moment of placement. When the detonation chain fires, the discharge effect scales with accumulated power. Concoctions also auto-detonate after a period determined by ammo consumed at placement — more ammo extends the active window, allowing greater accumulation and longer ongoing effect duration before the automatic discharge.

Siege Engine Operation — Siege engine companions (Ballista, Battering Ram, Catapult) can act on their own clock turns, but their base speed is extremely low. Without the Siege Engineer spending actions to advance them, they fire infrequently. The Siege Engineer’s move and minor toolkit exists largely to accelerate siege companions — quickening them, fuelling them with ammo for haste, and upgrading their next action via Siege Command.

Consequences — Consequence abilities generate Anguish on use and deal a deferred self-damage cost at the beginning of the Brute's next turn. Only the initial use generates Anguish; the deferred damage does not.

Reckless Abilities — Reckless abilities are powerful attacks that negate all active defenses and counter chances until the Raider's next turn. These abilities are further enhanced based on the total value of those active defenses at the moment of use.
Exertion — Exertion abilities have reduced accuracy. On a miss, the attack repeats targeting a random enemy and deals backbiting self-damage to the Berserker. This self-damage generates Anguish.

Rampage — Rampage accumulates as enemies are killed. Personal kills grant a higher Rampage bonus than team kills. Rampage enhances many of the Marauder's abilities, primarily scaling damage and speed.

Block Stacking — When the Viking has an ability prepared, each block made adds a charge to that specific ability. Multiple prepared abilities accumulate charges independently. When the ability fires, it consumes all stacks for enhanced damage or effect. Stacks are lost if the ability is disrupted.

Brink — Brink abilities become available for one turn after the Rager's cumulative damage dealt crosses a fixed threshold. This threshold tracks damage across multiple hits and turns. Once the threshold is crossed, unused Brink abilities expire at the end of the turn.
Purity Amplification — Purity abilities amplify in power each time they are used without triggering their cancellation condition. Each Purity has its own independent stack and cancellation condition.

Healing Threshold — The Cannibal can use threshold abilities when she has received enough healing that could actually be applied to her. Overhealing — healing above maximum health — does not count. The threshold accumulates across multiple heals. Some threshold abilities are prepared and activate automatically when the threshold is met; others require manual activation.

Massive Damage — Massive damage occurs when a single attack deals damage equal to or exceeding a set percentage of the target's maximum health. This threshold scales with target health rather than the Destroyer's stats.

Beast Forms are ongoing minor abilities that consume Anguish and provide continuous stat bonuses with additional effects. Only one form can be active at a time — activating a new form replaces the previous one immediately.

“To get to the king, you have to get through me.”
“By my liege and blade, I will not let you fall.”
“You shall see the light of Hugh. Accept its glory or burn by it.”
“Lightning is ideal for keeping your opponents off-balance, though some complain it is unpredictable.”
“Acid is ideal for destroying an opponent’s defenses, though some complain it works too slow.”
“You can get anything for the right price.”
“Let me tell you a joke.”
“I sing of death and despair. It is an all-too-common song.”

“The light will shine, and burn corruption away.”
“Have you met my friends yet?”
“Everything will be in balance.”
“These are the souls bound to us, the spirits that guide our path.”
“I have seen your fate written in the stars.”
“There are things from beyond our realm that can serve us very well. Or perhaps we shall serve them.”
“Pray for me now and at the hour of my death.”
“My faith shall protect me from illness.”
“And so God filled the flesh of man with his own divinity to protect us from the Calamities that faced the world.”
“You’re not dying on me. Not here. Not now.”

“By Hugh, these bastards won’t just stay buried, will they?”
“Look at him, swaying in the wind, like a carrion banner.”
“Your sins are so intricate, so delicious. You are quite the feast.”
“Sleep now. Let it all fade away.”
“Let me give you the mercy of oblivion”
“It is no longer reality that threatens you the most.”

During the war, the Trader States deployed scouts as the eyes of the Concord advance, mapping Abyssal territory and feeding intelligence back to the supply lines that won the war. Five years later, formal Scout units have largely dissolved, and most have traded military contracts for civilian work — surveyors, guides, pathfinders for merchant expeditions into the Abyssal Lands. The skills transfer cleanly. The pay is worse.

The Lion Woods Lodges are old institutions, older than the war, older than most of the nations that now send their wealthy to hunt there. Lodge Huntsmen follow a strict code — clean kills, respected quarry, proper ceremony. To outsiders it looks like theater. To a Huntsman, it is the only thing separating civilization from savagery.

The Trader States never romanticized archery. The crossbow was a tool of war, easier to train, easier to standardize, easier to supply. Crossbowmen served in regimented infantry units, and their discipline shows in everything they do — methodical, patient, institutional. Many now serve as caravan guards or city watch, bringing that same regimental precision to peacetime work.

Nobody teaches you to be a Stalker. You learn it from the Abyssal Lands themselves, from years of hunting things that hunt you back. Stalkers have a seedier reputation than most archers — they operate in moral grey areas, take contracts others won't, and rarely ask questions about their quarry. In a land full of desperate people, they are rarely short of work.

The Lodges of the Lion Woods did not consult the locals when they drew their boundaries. Poachers are what happens when people who have hunted these woods for generations are told they need a permit to feed their families. Some are purely opportunistic, selling to wealthy buyers who want exotic meat without the Lodge fees. Others see themselves as something closer to resistors.

The Hunter's Guild expanded its mandate after the war, turning its tracking expertise toward war criminals, Abyssal collaborators, and fugitives. It pays well and carries a veneer of legitimacy. The reality is messier — a Trader States bounty hunter pursuing a Dynasian war criminal is a spy to Dynasian eyes, and the Abyssal Lands have no authority to appeal to. Most Bounty Hunters develop a pragmatic relationship with moral complexity early in their careers.

Dynasia's Marksmen were its answer to the massed enemy formations of the Abyssal war — elite archers trained to break lines, take officers, and hold positions against overwhelming numbers. They carried the same cultural weight as English longbowmen, celebrated in ballads and given honors. Post-war, many struggle with the gap between that reputation and the grinding reality of peacetime, where their skills feel outsized for the problems at hand.

Archery contests exploded in popularity in the five years since the Concord's victory — a way to celebrate survival, maintain martial culture, and give veterans somewhere to put their edge. Sharpshooters are the products of that culture, trained not in war but in competition, where consistency and nerve under pressure are everything. They lack the battlefield experience of Marksmen but often surpass them in pure technical precision.

Falconry in Dynasia is older than the GodKing's church and considerably more honest about what it is — a display of wealth, patience, and mastery. Noble families have maintained their lines of trained birds for generations, and the Falconer subclass reflects that aristocratic lineage. Outside Dynasia, Falconers are curiosities, their methods considered elaborate and their birds an unnecessary extravagance. Inside Dynasia, a Falconer without noble blood is almost unheard of.

The Toxophilites do not belong to any nation and are not interested in your war. Theirs is a tradition of archery as devotion — the bow as instrument, the shot as meditation, accuracy as a form of self-knowledge. Masters pass the tradition to single students over years of rigorous study. Most archers find them insufferable. Most archers also secretly wish they could shoot like them.
Ameliorate Suffering – Ameliorates effects of damage afflictions on target ally (Balladeer)
Call of the Earth Guard – Grants all allies enhanced earth resistance if the balladeer’s earth resistance is higher, requires preparation (Balladeer)
Earth Song – Chord that grants earth damage and resistance (Balladeer)
Emergency Regeneration – Grant target ally regeneration until they are no longer endangered (Balladeer)
Momentary Earth Shield – Grants ally earth shield until the end of their next turn (Balladeer)
Reinforce Litany – Refreshes the duration of all active litanies on the target without adding stacks, granting extra time to reapply. (Balladeer)
Dark Empowerment, Momentary – Target ally gains dark empowerment until end of turn (Dirge Singer)
Dark Melody – Gain mana, requires only dischords in song (Dirge Singer)
Painful Song – Increases the power and potency of damage afflictions applied to enemies affected by song (Dirge Singer)
Shared Vampirism – Next life drain ability also heals targeted ally (Dirge Singer)
Stunning Cacophony – Cacophony ability — stuns target enemy based on affliction count. (Dirge Singer)
Acid Reflection – Reflect next earth damage taken by unit (Balladeer)
Corroding Song – Dischord that causes an earth bleed and lowers earth resist (Balladeer)
Corruption Revitalization – Reduces corruption on target ally and heals based on amount removed. (Balladeer)
Fortification Note – Buff that grants target fortification and adds them to audience (Balladeer)
Litany of Affliction – Applies a stacking litany that lowers the target's affliction resistance. Duration resets and value increases per cast, up to 5 stacks. (Balladeer)
Litany of Protection – Applies a stacking litany that increases the target's defense. Duration resets and value increases per cast, up to 5 stacks. (Balladeer)
Litany of Restoration – Applies a stacking litany that grants the target regeneration. Duration resets and value increases per cast, up to 5 stacks. (Balladeer)
Vicious Reflection – Reflect damage of next critical hit that targets unit (Balladeer)
Decisive Purge – Purges target ally. Triggers following an enemy death or becoming endangered. (Dirge Singer)
Decisive Rejuvenation – Heals and regenerates target ally. Triggers following an enemy death or becoming endangered. (Dirge Singer)
Decrepit Refrain – Lower damage of all enemies in audience for a period (Dirge Singer)
Disturbing Cacophony – Cacophony ability — disrupts all enemies, scaled by affliction count. (Dirge Singer)
Fatal Reflection – Reflect next death effect that targets unit (Dirge Singer)
Moon Reflection – Reflect next dark damage taken by unit (Dirge Singer)
Song of Torment – Increases all aspects of afflictions used by allies affected by song (Dirge Singer)
Acid Salt Shot – Ranged earth attack with piercing (Balladeer)
Ballad of Mountains – Earth magic versus row and grant all allies earth damage add with next attack (Balladeer)
Ballad of Storms – Air magic storm that grants allies lightning damage to next attack (Balladeer)
Blessing Chorus – Ranged attack with blessed damage and delay self. Allies’ attacks against target have blessed damage until next turn (Balladeer)
Heavy Chorus – Ranged attack with increased damage and delay self. Allies’ attacks against target have increased damage until next turn (Balladeer)
Litany of Blood – Applies a stacking litany that deals untyped bleed to the target. Duration resets and value increases per cast, up to 5 stacks. (Balladeer)
Litany of Power – Applies a stacking litany that increases the target's damage. Duration resets and value increases per cast, up to 5 stacks. (Balladeer)
Litany of Illusion – Applies a stacking litany that increases the target's illusory damage. Duration resets and value increases per cast, up to 5 stacks. (Balladeer)
Rock Chorus – Ranged attack with earth damage add and delay self. Allies’ attacks against target have earth damage add until next turn (Balladeer)
Rock Note – Ranged earth note that adds target to audience (Balladeer)
Rootsong – Ranged attack that deals earth damage, slows target, and adds them to audience (Balladeer)
Corrupt Cacophony – Cacophony ability — corrupt magic attack against target, scaled by non-damaging afflictions applied since the Dirge Singer's last turn. (Dirge Singer)
Dark Cacophony – Cacophony ability — dark magic attack against all enemies, scaled by affliction count. (Dirge Singer)
Decisive Resurrection – Raises a fallen ally. Triggers only following an enemy death or when an enemy becomes endangered. (Dirge Singer)
Doom Dirge – Applies a cull countdown to all enemies. (Dirge Singer)
Doom Lyrics – Applies a cull countdown to a single enemy. (Dirge Singer)
Drain Corruption – Ranged attack that drains life based on corruption on target (Dirge Singer)
Echoing Cacophony – Cacophony ability — multi-hit magic attack against random targets, scaled by affliction count. (Dirge Singer)
Ghost Note – Grants ally intangible and countdown heal until next turn, adds ally to audience (Dirge Singer)
Seventh Song Refrain – Drains all enemies in audience and spreads heal among all allies in audience (Dirge Singer)
Storm Cacophony – Cacophony ability — air magic storm attack, scaled by affliction count. (Dirge Singer)
Vampiric Cacophony – Cacophony ability — life drain attack against target, scaled by affliction count. (Dirge Singer)
Vampiric Note – Ranged note that drains life from target and adds them to the audience. (Dirge Singer)
Wail of the Banshee – Channeled dark magic attack against all enemies. Damage and culling threshold both increase over the channel duration. Can be interrupted. (Dirge Singer)

Cacophony abilities scale in power based on the number of unique non-damaging debuff actions applied to any unit by any ally between the end of the Dirge Singer's previous turn and the end of his current turn. Each distinct debuff action adds one stack, up to a maximum of 10. The count resets at the end of the Dirge Singer's turn.
Call of the Water Guard – Grants all allies enhanced water resistance if the drummer’s water resistance is higher, requires preparation (Drummer)
Disrupting Song – Increases chances of enemies in the audience to be disrupted. (Drummer)
Favor of Nergal – “Nergal, who rules the darkness, grant me your favor” – Heals target ally and grants dark damage add (Drummer)
Greater Favor – Increase the value of damage adds present on the target until next turn (Drummer)
Ice Song – Grants water damage and resistance to audience (Drummer)
Steady Attack – Reduce damage range of next attack by enemy (Drummer)
Drowning Song – Causes enemies in the audience to take ongoing water damage and have lower water resistance (Drummer)
Favor of Enlil – Heals and quickens target ally and grants air damage add (Drummer)
Favor of Shamash – Heals and purges target ally and grants light damage add (Drummer)
Favor of Tammuz – “Tammuz, father of the earth, grant me your favor” – Heals target ally and grants earth damage add (Drummer)
Heavy Note – Grants target ally increased minimum damage and a chance to disrupt with next attack; adds target to the audience (Drummer)
Steady Recovery – Grant all allies a short duration regeneration (Drummer)
Ballad of the Waves – Water magic attack versus all that grants all allies water damage add with next attack (Drummer)
Crashing Waves – Magic water storm attack (Drummer)
Deafening Refrain – Heavy damage to audience while distracting and disrupting them. (Drummer)
Disrupting Note – Ranged attack that has a chance to disrupt and adds target to audience (Drummer)
Favor of Marduk – “Marduk, Lord of the Seas, grant me your favor” – Prepared heal for the entire team that also grants water damage add (Drummer)
Frost Note – Ranged water attack that adds target to audience (Drummer)
Heavy Refrain – Targets all members of the audience, dealing damage and delaying (Drummer)
Iceberg – Water magic attack versus all with a chance to proc prone (Drummer)
Sudden Storm Bolt – Magic air attack against random enemy with sudden and disruption (Drummer)
Thundering Beat – Air magic attack versus all enemies that stuns. (Drummer)
Trident Beam – Magic attack versus three random columns, dealing, in order, earth, water, and air damage. (Drummer)
Tsunami Shot – Ranged attack with a chance to proc water damage versus all enemies (Drummer)
Wave Chorus – Water ranged attack that grants allies water damage add to their next attack (Drummer)

Every tribe has them — the biggest, the strongest, the ones who lead from the front because nothing has ever stopped them yet. Brutes are not a tradition so much as a fact of tribal life, found in Horse Tribes and Wolf Tribes and every desperate settlement scratching out existence in the Abyssal Lands. Civilized soldiers call them unsophisticated. They are usually saying this while retreating.

When the war ended, not everyone received liberation equally. Some peoples found themselves displaced twice — first by the Abyssals, then by the Concord's redrawing of the world. Vandal bands formed in the margins of the Abyssal Lands from these dispossessed groups, united less by tribe or blood than by shared grievance. Their destructive reputation is not entirely unearned, but neither is it the whole story.

The Trader States and Dynasia both discovered the same uncomfortable truth during the war — sometimes you need someone who simply does not care what they break. Destroyers were recruited from tribal warriors and shaped into military specialists, siege-breakers and fortification-wreckers deployed where finesse was beside the point. They occupy an uneasy place, too institutionalized for the tribes, too savage for polite military society.

Somewhere in the deep tribal territories, certain warriors began teaching that rage was not a weapon to be unleashed but a fire to be tended. Fury lodges exist quietly within and between tribes, passing their discipline from master to student with something approaching monastic rigor. Where the Berserker loses himself in battle, the Fury never does. Outsiders who expect a screaming savage are often the last ones surprised.

The old Valisian crews have sailed and raided and fought since before the Confederacy existed, and they intend to keep doing so long after political arrangements come and go. Vikings carry the weight of that cultural identity proudly — the longships, the reputation, the songs. Paradoxically they are among the most loyal to the Grand Commodore, because the Confederacy is their institution, built on their tradition, and they have no intention of letting newer members dilute it.

Land-bound and relentless, Marauders measure themselves in kills and territory held. They exist across the Abyssal Lands in various tribal and non-tribal forms, defined less by culture than by philosophy — that dominance is proven through accumulation, that every battle is an opportunity to add to a tally that matters. Some tribes regard Marauder traditions with respect. Others consider them a corruption of what honorable warfare means.

The practice exists across many tribes and outside the tribal structure entirely, and it is rarely what outsiders imagine. In its traditional form it is ritual — consuming the strength of a worthy enemy, honoring them through incorporation. Cults have taken that ritual and hollowed it into something genuinely vile, which has poisoned the reputation of practitioners who still follow the old ways. The distinction matters enormously to those who observe it. It matters very little to those who fear them.

The Valis Confederacy produced a particular type of fighter during the war — one who could shift on a heartbeat from disciplined defense to reckless overwhelming assault. Raiders trained that instinct into a fighting style, the sudden lurch from shield to sword that breaks formations and unnerves veterans. Post-war, many Raiders have drifted into mercenary work in the Abyssal Lands, where that volatile quality is either prized or feared depending on who's hiring.

The Berserker does not choose to lose control. That is the point. The tradition, found across tribal cultures in various forms, is built around a fighter whose rage responds to damage, to threat, to the heat of battle — reactive and escalating. Tribes that produce Berserkers regard them with a mixture of pride and wariness. They are invaluable in the right circumstances. The right circumstances require careful management.

Every animal tribe tells stories of warriors who went so deep into their totem identity that they stopped being entirely human. Most are legends. Some are not. Beastlords emerge rarely, across all tribes, and when they do they tend to outgrow the tribe that produced them — not through rejection but through transcendence. They carry their tribal origins with them but belong to something older and wilder, a connection to the animal world that no lodge or tradition fully owns or understands.

A slow-building setup caster who places runes across eight types and charges them through active spellcasting. When runes prime, he fires runespells that combine them for escalating payoffs — trading early vulnerability for a mid-to-late board state that punishes enemies on multiple fronts simultaneously.

The defensive anchor of the Runemage family, specializing in defense runes that proc when attacked and earth magic that punishes aggression. He builds damage shields, stacks fortification, and redirects enemy attention — a runemage who invites attacks rather than avoiding them.

A fire-and-reaction specialist who layers trigger runes onto enemies and detonates them for chain damage. He excels at punishing enemies who act predictably, converting their own procs and parries against them, and scaling his piercing through exploitation of negative proc triggers.

An earth-focused runemage who pairs enchantment runes with a golem companion to create a layered defensive presence. He can fortify and redirect damage through his golem, convert a dying companion into personal survivability through Golem Armor, and punish enemies who bypass his defenses with reflected damage.

A water-and-affliction specialist who escalates conditions over time, with particular mastery of countdowns, hexes, and stacking water effects. Festering makes purging a liability — removed afflictions return stronger — and his alone toolkit rewards surviving after his allies fall.

A runemage who strips enemy enchantments and turns them into resources, damage, or afflictions. He punishes enchanted enemies, converts his rune board into a single devastating attack through Rune to Oblivion, and can flip the game state by stealing and weaponizing what enemies rely on.

A trap-focused arcane specialist who builds mana-reactive field hazards and punishes enemy spellcasting and action patterns. He generates and redirects mana through traps and switches, rewarding dense trap setups with the Trap Spotting capstone that converts each activation into action economy.

An elemental piercing specialist who focuses runemages' natural elemental identity into a concentrated beam of resistances-ignored damage. He builds prisms for deferred area detonations, charges his elemental runes for enhanced power, and covers the team with elemental shielding and empowerments.

A proc amplifier who loads allies and enemies with damage runes and triggers them through Stone Glyph attacks and Glyphic Onslaught. He converts stacked procs into multi-hit chain attacks and distributes rune effects across the party, rewarding dense proc setups with escalating damage.

A timing rune master who builds countdown engines, manipulates their timers, and squeezes maximum value before consuming them. Remnants of Fate converts every countdown — allied or enemy — into mana, making him a resource engine in any fight heavy with time-based effects.

The pinnacle runemage, commanding multiple power runes, a three-rune runespell, and a self-reinforcing earth countdown trio that multiplies in power when maintained together. He preserves preparation through the Conserve Preparation capstone and sustains himself through personal countdown engines, building toward overwhelming late-game board states.

Companion Mana — The Conjurer works in concert with her companion, using its mana pool to enhance her own abilities. Many of her abilities function on their own but become stronger or gain additional effects when companion mana is available to draw from

Dark Spirits — The Occultist manipulates dark and light spirits to protect herself and allies with powerful retaliation abilities. These spirits deal a variety of damage types beyond standard elemental damage, and channeling them further shifts her alignment. Her retaliation suite covers multiple damage types and can be granted to any unit.

Attendant Abilities — Attendant abilities are prepared abilities that reserve mana while held. They all trigger simultaneously when the Shaman's companion scores a critical hit. Multiple Attendants can be prepared at once — the longer the Shaman waits for the critical, the greater the combined effect when it finally fires.

Balanced Alignment — Unlike most other Binders, the Medium is strongest near the center of the alignment scale. Her most powerful abilities require Balanced scale position, and she gains bonuses for remaining within the 1/4 range on either side.

Animation — The Animist infuses her companion with spiritual energy. Animation abilities buff the companion so that its next attack carries an additional effect. These effects do not fire until the companion's next turn, meaning they can be thwarted by defeating the companion before it acts.

Endangered Enhancements — Precarious abilities have two tiers of power. The first tier activates when either the Spiritualist or the target is endangered. The second, more powerful tier activates when both the Spiritualist and the target are simultaneously endangered.
Multi-Critical — Many of the Astrologer's abilities gain benefits for each separate enemy they score a critical hit against during a single use.

Corrupt Power — The Vizier deals corrupt damage to her own allies as a side effect of her most powerful abilities. Many of her abilities scale with total corruption present on the battlefield — on enemies, allies, and herself.

Sanity Cost — The Alienist deliberately accumulates illusory damage on herself to unlock her most powerful abilities and fuel her damage scaling. Several abilities require that she has taken sufficient illusory damage to use.

Pacts — Pact abilities are powerful ongoing commitments that each provide two bonuses and one drawback. Only one Pact can be active at a time — activating a new Pact replaces the current one. All Pacts reserve mana while active.
Litany abilities apply stacking duration effects. Each cast of the same litany refreshes the duration and increases the value, up to a maximum of 5 stacks.
Favor abilities call upon named deities to heal a target ally and grant them an elemental damage add corresponding to that deity's domain.

The Spy can don disguises in battle. He must be hidden to put on a disguise. Each disguise grants both advantages and disadvantages as he emulates the pretended role. While disguised, each disguise ability can be activated a second time to trigger a unique effect — but doing so removes the disguise.
As long as enemies cannot target the Mountebank — due to avert, scorn, or hidden — he can use veiled abilities that are stronger than normal
Entourage abilities grant a free attack to an ally with a provoke rider causing the next enemy to target that ally, plus a varying defensive buff to protect them from that attention.

The Muse can unlock powerful abilities following a resurrection. Most Epiphany abilities are minor or move actions that can be completed in the same turn the Muse or an ally provides the resurrection. The most powerful Epiphany ability is a major action that requires an ally to have performed a resurrection since the Muse's last turn.

Unleash — The Initiate has abilities that grow stronger the longer he remains in the same form, but the ability only becomes unleashed when he changes form. Unleash value accumulates while holding a form and is spent on unleashed abilities when a form transition occurs.
Impact — The Pugilist uses impact abilities that require that he struck an enemy in the previous turn. These abilities can only target whoever the Pugilist attacked the previous turn.

Matching — The Skirmisher can utilize matching abilities that allow him to use the statistic of enemies if their statistic is higher. Matching defenses last for a short time, while matching offenses take place with their attack.
Glancing Mastery — Due to their training, Stone Fists can deal impressive glancing blows to enemies with high defense and that are intangible, and can cause other effects with these glancing blows.

Arrival — While most who hide from their enemies prefer to stay hidden, the Infiltrator uses abilities that expose him to cause effects. These abilities can never conserve hidden, though they may gain other benefits if hidden would otherwise be conserved.
Purity — The Ascetic gains access to powerful abilities if he is not affected by any affliction. Some of these abilities are restricted to specific forms.

Ability Chains — The Thunderfist can use ability chains. Second tier abilities in these chains have a requirement of a precursor action. All of the abilities make the class very synergistic with itself, though precursors can be found in other classes to allow more variety.

Form Shifting — The Drunken Master excels when he is rapidly changing from one form to another. Some abilities are stronger based on the total stages of forms he has shifted in the current turn, while other abilities are only available if he has shifted a minimum number of steps.

A self-destructive dark spellcaster who draws power from her own suffering. She bleeds herself to fuel magic, weaponizes backbiting damage, and unlocks her most dangerous abilities only when endangered — a glass cannon who gets deadlier the closer she is to death.

A cursed healer who turns purging into a weapon. She applies malediction to prime enemies for devastating purge payoffs, spreads afflictions between foes, and generates divinity through the same heals and purges that dismantle enemy debuff stacks — rewarding aggressive support play over passive restoration.

The most defensively oriented class in the game, sacrificing nearly all offense for impenetrable protection. He combines the Knight's guard relationship with the Monk's chakra system to absorb, redirect, and punish incoming damage — closing chakras as a shield resource and building passive defense through deliberate restraint.

A hypnotic controller who locks enemies in place through sustained channeling. She combines the Bard's audience manipulation with the Psychic's influence system, using set-duration channels that build powerful end-of-channel payoffs — rewarding patience and disruption resistance over raw damage output.

A versatile skirmisher who fights equally well at melee and ranged distance. He builds accuracy stacks by alternating between sword and bow, with each weapon type setting up the other — a class built around deliberate rhythm rather than specialization.

An air-powered melee fighter who weaponizes her own forcefield. She drains her damage shield through Intensify abilities to deliver air attacks, control effects, and retaliatory damage — spending defense as offense and regenerating it through combat aggression.

A versatile conjurer who supplements traditional companion play with powerful Calling abilities that channel summon energy directly. He combines Binder alignment management with Runemage rune customization to enhance and vary his companions, with Lingering Essence rewarding rapid Calling chains and smooth transitions between summons.

A brutal opportunist who sets up stuns and flanks to land devastating follow-up strikes. He combines Barbarian rage with Rogue advantage to exploit enemy vulnerability — stunning enemies to generate resources, quickening himself through Cruel Momentum when enemies lose their turns, and hitting hardest when foes are most helpless.

Cruor Magic - The Blood Mage gains power from blood, and when she becomes endangered from her own blood loss, her power increases. She can unlock her most dangerous abilities only when her health is critically low.
Blood is Mana – A portion of health is spent instead of mana to cast spells.
Redirected Maladies – Whenever she purges an affliction, she gains increased affliction power.

Martial Patience – The Guardian builds stacking defense on turns where no damage-dealing ability is used. All stacks are lost when the Guardian uses a damage-dealing ability. Counters and reactions do not remove stacks.
Sustained Trance – Channel Power passive also increases channel duration.

Alternating Combat - The Ranger builds accuracy stacks by alternating between melee and ranged attacks, with each weapon type setting up the other. His kit mirrors across both ranges, rewarding deliberate rhythm over pure specialization.

Blade to Bow – The Ranger gains stacks that improve accuracy each time he switches between ranged and melee attacks. The number of stacks that can be held is based on skill level. Stacks are lost when the Ranger uses either two melee or two ranged abilities consecutively.
Intensify - The Shock Trooper weaponizes her own damage shield through Intensify abilities, which drain the damage shield as a cost to deliver powerful air attacks and control effects.
Sparking Forcefield – Whenever the Shock Trooper loses a threshold amount of damage shield, she deals air damage to a random enemy. The threshold resets after triggering.
Calling - Calling abilities channel summon power directly without a companion present, providing powerful effects.
Lingering Essence – For two turns after any companion leaves the battlefield, the Summoner gains increased magic power and summoning power.
Cruel Momentum – Whenever an enemy misses its turn due to the stunned condition, the Thug is quickened.
Aura of Calm – Frightened allies cannot cower. Can be sustained (Lantern Bearer)
Illuminated Sharp – Ranged note that illuminates target enemy and adds them to the audience. (Lantern Bearer)
Imposing Brilliance – Averts all enemies from a target illuminated ally and refreshes that ally's song duration. (Lantern Bearer)
Lantern Pulse – Disenchant all enemies of hidden status (Lantern Bearer)
Master of Light – Grants an illuminated ally a light add with next attack (Lantern Bearer)
Solar Song – Chord that grants increased light resist and damage (Lantern Bearer)
Guardian Epiphany – Enchant ally that was resurrected this turn with damage shield and fortification (Muse)
Instant Epiphany – Quicken ally that was resurrected this turn (Muse)
Preparation Epiphany – Grants mana to ally that was resurrected this turn (Muse)
Restoration Epiphany – Heal ally that was resurrected this turn and grant it regeneration (Muse)
Reverberating Reflection – Grant ally retaliation based on damage reflected since last turn (Muse)
Song of Mana – Increases mana generation of allied audience (Muse)
Improved Overheal – Increase value of next overheal effect (Diva)
Overcharge Evocation – Consume 5% of maximum mana to grant extra air damage based on amount spent to next magic attack (Diva)
Overcharge Restoration – Consume 5% of maximum mana to grant extra healing based on amount to next heal (Diva)
Purified Flesh – Purge ally following healing them to full (Diva)
Regeneration Remembrance – Refreshes regeneration on a single target (Diva)
Shield Chant – Channeled ability generating damage shield on ally (Diva)
Dark Guard – Enhances dark resistance of ally (Mountebank)
Deflect Attention – The next time the Mountebank targets an ally (including self), that ally gains scorn. (Mountebank)
Nocturnal Song – Chord that enhances dark resist and adds dark damage (Mountebank)
Veil Ally – Scorn and quicken target ally (Mountebank)
Veil Enemy – Avert and flank target enemy (Mountebank)
Veiled Affliction – Lower target’s affliction resistance, magic resistance, and defense. Requires target is averted (Mountebank)
Avert and Hide – Averts an enemy. If averted from all enemies, become hidden (Spy)
Disguise Aversion – Avert target enemy. Requires disguise (Spy)
Remove Disguise – Disenchants any current disguise abilities (Spy)
Song of Evasion – Chord that grants increased evasion to allied audience (Spy)
Throw Voice – Flank target enemy. Requires hidden (Spy)
Aura of Clarity – Creates an aura that protects against illusory damage. Can be maintained for reduced cost (Lantern Bearer)
Aura of Light – Creates an aura that causes illuminate status to enemies (Lantern Bearer)
Cursed Song – Reduces critical chance and proc chance of audience members (Lantern Bearer)
Elucidating Pulse – Enhance accuracy and critical chance of all allies. Can be maintained (Lantern Bearer)
Irradiating Song – Causes enemy audience to take light bleed and lowers light resistance (Lantern Bearer)
Mass Light Empowerment – Enchant all allies with light empowerment (Lantern Bearer)
Radiant Gleam – Prepared accuracy weakness and delay versus single and can be sustained to repeat (Lantern Bearer)
Sun Reflection – Reflect next light damage taken by unit (Lantern Bearer)
Barrier Heal – Heal ally and grant it barrier (Muse)
Frost Epiphany – Grant ally that was resurrected this turn water damage add (Muse)
Inspired Remedy – Purge ally of afflictions and grant mana based on afflictions purged (Muse)
Lightning Reflection – Reflect next air damage taken by unit (Muse)
Possession Epiphany – Possess ally that was resurrected during this turn (Muse)
Recovery Field – Heal all allies. Can be sustained for reduced cost (Muse)
Reverberating Defenses – Heal ally and grant damage shield with amplification (Muse)
Reverberating Song – Chord that grants untyped retaliation to ally audience (Muse)
Encouraging Note – Grants a free attack to a random ally in the audience with a provoke and a quicken. (Diva)
Enduring Song – Grants audience enduring. Members are removed when they benefit from enduring (Diva)
Mana Heal – Single target heal that grants mana surge based on overheal (Diva)
Performance Heal – Heal self. Overheals gained by each ally (Diva)
Personal Escort – Grants a free attack to an ally with a provoke and damage reduction until end of their next turn. (Diva)
Shield Refrain – Grant allies in audience damage shield (Diva)
Standing Ovation – Grants a free attack to an ally in the audience with a provoke and enduring until next hit. Song mechanic. (Diva)
Aversion Refrain – Averts all enemies in audience (Mountebank)
Darkness Heal – Prepared heal that grants target hidden (Mountebank)
Draw Their Eyes – All flanked enemies are delayed and averted from the Mountebank. (Mountebank)
Disappearing Note – Causes hidden on ally and adds it to audience (Mountebank)
Obscuring Song – Causes dark damage over times, lowers dark resist (Mountebank)
Slow Song – Dischord that lowers speed of enemy audience (Mountebank)
Slowing Poison – Applies slow poison to attacks (Mountebank)
Unstable Poison – Applies a poison to attacks that adds a random damage amount and flanks the target (Mountebank)
Veiled Heal – Heal target ally. Requires and consumes hidden (Mountebank)
Brisk Note – Grant haste to ally and add it to audience (Spy)
False Information – Possess random enemy to attack target and add the random enemy to audience (Spy)
Flanking Refrain – Causes all enemies in audience to become flanked (Spy)
Gather Intelligence – Next attack by any unit against averted target is a critical hit (Spy)
Lullaby – Chance to cause incapacitated status on enemy audience on spy’s turn (Spy)
Music Box – Creates a trap on field that causes next three units to act to join audience (Spy)
Significant Misdirection – Next attack against Spy targets an ally instead and attacking enemy is flanked after (Spy)
Brightness – Magic light attack versus all that causes blind (Lantern Bearer)
Bullseye Lantern – Single target light magic that afflicts target with illuminate (Lantern Bearer)
Eliminate Corruption – Damages any enemy suffering corruption and reduces corruption on all allies (Lantern Bearer)
Purifying Pulse – Prepared heal that reduces corrupted and can be sustained to repeat (Lantern Bearer)
Radiant Pulse – Prepared light magic damage versus all and can be sustained to repeat (Lantern Bearer)
Radiant Ray – Prepared light magic damage versus single and can be sustained to repeat (Lantern Bearer)
Revealing Radiance – Creates an aura that can be sustained that drains mana, lowers dodge, and deals light damage (Lantern Bearer)
Shining Lantern – Channeled light magic damage that illuminates and blinds target (Lantern Bearer)
Sunshine Refrain – Deals light damage to all enemies in audience and causes illuminated. (Lantern Bearer)
Turn Light to Pain – Purge illuminated from self and deal magic light damage to all enemies (Lantern Bearer)
Vengeant Radiance – Creates an aura that grants light retaliation to all allies and reduces corruption (Lantern Bearer)
Amplifying Sharp – Ranged attack with amplify that adds target to audience. Can only target enemies not in audience (Muse)
Chorus of Absolution – Possess any ally revived before next turn to make powerful attack (Muse)
Evening Chant – Lowers enemy health and raises ally health until the average values are equal. Channeled (Muse)
Icy Spikes – Water magic attack versus all that grants team water retaliation (Muse)
Inspirational Critical – Ranged attack that quickens and enhances damage of audience on critical (Muse)
Note of Life – Raises target and makes it a part of audience (Muse)
Rebirth Refrain – All allies in audience gain revive on death proc for a period (Muse)
Resurrection Pulse – Generates a resurrection effect that triggers 3 times with periods in between (Muse)
Reverberating Sound – Magic attack and gain retaliation based on damage dealt (Muse)
Supreme Resurrection – Raises target to a high health total (Muse)
Violent Reprisal – Grants powerful untyped retaliation to entire team (Muse)
Champion’s Note – Grants an ally damage shield and compels all enemies to attack ally (Diva)
Command Performance – Grants all allies a free attack. Each ally taunts a random enemy. Each ally also receives a dodge enhancement. (Diva)

Disruption Scream – Channeled magic ability against all that disrupts. The disruption power starts a certain level and increases over time. Enemy magic prepared after the scream begins only compares to the channel that has happened during its preparation. (Diva)
Existential Howl – Channeled magic attack that adds all enemies to audience over the period of the channel (Diva)
Rocky Refrain – Earth magic damage versus all enemies in audience (Diva)
Share Spotlight – Grants a single ally a free attack with a provoke and damage shield. (Diva)
Shatter Note – Ranged attack with shatter that disrupts and adds to audience (Diva)
Shattering Scream – Channeled magic ability with shatter (Diva)
Solo Spotlight – Channeled arcane attack that continues until disrupted. Requires alone (Diva)
Sonic Sphere – Magic attack versus all that causes distract (Diva)
Spotlight Performance – Channeled light magic attack against all enemies, simultaneously provoking them to attack the Diva. Lasts until the Diva takes damage. (Diva)
Temporal Refrain – Delay all enemies in audience and quicken all allies in audience (Diva)
Averting Shot – Ranged attack requiring hidden that averts target (Mountebank)
Darkness Trick – Ranged dark attack with piercing that causes blindness (Mountebank)
Midnight Refrain – Dark magic attack against all enemies in audience (Mountebank)
Poisonous Sharp – Ranged attack with poisonous that adds target to audience (Mountebank)
Possessive Note – Ranged attack that possesses target and adds them to audience (Mountebank)
Shadowy Note – Dark ranged attack that adds target to audience (Mountebank)
Veiled Arrows – Ranged attack with blind against all flanked enemies (Mountebank)
Veiled Blast – Dark magic attack versus all averted enemies. Removes aversion (Mountebank)

Veiled Domination – Possesses all averted enemies. (Mountebank)
Archer Disguise – Grants spy bonuses and penalties as he emulates an archer. Requires hidden. Can be removed to make a distant ranged attack (Spy)
Aversion Shot – Ranged attack against averted enemy (Spy)
Disguised Strike – Flank enemy then make a melee attack against it. Requires disguised. (Spy)
Flanking Sharp – Ranged attack against flanked enemy that adds it to audience (Spy)

Soldier Disguise – Grants spy bonuses and penalties as he emulates a soldier. Requires hidden. Can be removed to make a powerful melee attack (Spy)
Sonic Trap – Trap that deals piercing magic damage to target that disrupts and distracts (Spy)

Wizard Disguise – Grants spy bonuses and penalties as he emulates a wizard. Requires hidden. Can be removed to make a magic attack against all enemies (Spy)

In a world still finding its way out of the dark, the Lantern Bearer is less a title than a calling — a Bard who has stopped performing for recognition and started performing because the world needs light and they happen to know how to make it. They carry music, and warmth, and something harder to name into places that have been without those things for too long. They are the apex of what a Bard can become, not through technical mastery alone but through a quality of presence that has nothing to do with technique. Lance Hadley, young and optimistic and native to the darkest territory in the known world, is perhaps a natural candidate — though he would be the last to say so.

Nobody decides to become a Muse. The reputation accumulates around certain rare individuals whose presence seems to unlock something in the people around them — artists who create better work, soldiers who fight with more conviction, grieving people who find unexpected reserves of hope. Whether this is a form of magic or simply the effect of an exceptionally rare kind of personality is a question that tends to bore the people it most applies to. They are usually too busy helping someone else to discuss it.

In every major city, there are performers whose talent has elevated them into something approaching social currency. The Diva aspires to that status — the celebrated voice that powerful people compete to host, whose presence at a gathering signals the host's importance as much as any political alliance. The reality is more complicated. A Diva without a patron is simply a very talented person without income, and the patrons who collect them do not always remember that the instrument they prize is also a person.

The Wagon Folk have traveled every road in the known world since before any of the current nations drew their borders, bound by ancient pacts to keep moving and to harm no community they pass through. The Mountebank is their contribution to the performing arts — part musician, part trickster, part merchant of small miracles. They deal in sleight of hand and misdirection, in the gap between what an audience believes and what is actually happening. This makes them either charming or deeply unsettling depending on the mark.

Every nation with interests in the Abyssal Lands needs eyes it can trust, and the Spy discovered long ago that a lute is better cover than almost anything else. People talk around performers. They forget they are being listened to. Some Spies maintain genuine loyalty to the nation that trained them, though determining which nation that is can be genuinely difficult when the same operative has accepted commissions from three different employers. Others have dispensed with loyalty entirely and sell information to whoever pays. The cold war developing between the Concord nations has made both varieties extremely busy.

The galleys of Valis run on rhythm. The Drummer sits at the heart of the ship, setting the pace of the oars, and in the tradition of the old Valisian faith they are doing something more than keeping time — they are invoking Marduk, Enlil, and Tammuz, the Trinity whose blessing keeps the sea from swallowing the crew whole. The Pnang, arriving from the Far West centuries ago with a strangely similar faith, integrated into this tradition more smoothly than anyone expected. Whether that convergence means something, nobody has satisfactorily explained.

The Trader States reward excellence in many forms, and the Balladeer occupies a strange position in that system — artists kept by guild masters and merchant princes to compose odes to their greatness. The work requires genuine talent and produces genuine art, which makes the compromise all the more uncomfortable. In recent years, Balladeers have been asked to do more than flatter their patrons — to smooth over supply line failures, to reframe massacres as necessities, to make the history of the war sound cleaner than it was. Most comply. The ones who don't find new patrons quickly.

The church of Alister High has elaborate ceremonies for the dead, and the Dirge Singer emerged from those ceremonies as a specialized role — voices trained to carry grief in a register that feels almost liturgical. Five years after the war's end, with so many dead to mourn across every nation, Dirge Singers have rarely been busier. Some have wandered far from Dynasia, finding that grief is universal even when the specific prayers are not.

Every court needs someone willing to say the unsayable, and Dynasia's feudal structure produced the Jester as a formalized answer to that need. The fool's motley is a license — to mock the powerful, to speak truths that would cost anyone else their head, to make the GodKing's nobility laugh at themselves. The license has limits, and every Jester knows exactly where those limits are. The good ones push right up against them. The great ones occasionally step over, and either survive or don't.

Nobody hired them to be there. The Minstrel shows up at the inn, passes the hat, and moves on before anyone can ask where they came from. In the Abyssal Lands, where joy is scarce and memories of the occupation are still raw, Minstrels have become something quietly essential — traveling folk musicians carrying songs between isolated settlements, keeping oral traditions alive that no institution bothered to preserve. They are not celebrated. They are needed, which is better.

The academies of the Trader States teach the Conjurer tradition with an emphasis on containment. Before any student is permitted to reach through the veil, they spend years learning the safeguards — the circles, the bindings, the precise language of compulsion that keeps summoned entities from turning on their summoner. The Conjurer considers this rigor a mark of professionalism that distinguishes them from every other Binder tradition. Other Binder traditions consider the Conjurer dangerously overconfident in their circles.

Nobody taught the Occultist. That is both their distinction and their danger. Driven by obsession rather than institutional training, the Occultist pursues veil knowledge through whatever texts, ruins, and ill-advised experiments they can access, accumulating understanding the hard way. With the veil weakened since Abaddon's summoning, self-taught practitioners are finding it easier than ever to make contact — and considerably harder to maintain control of what answers. The Occultist tradition produces remarkable breakthroughs and remarkable disasters in roughly equal measure.

The tribes of the Abyssal Lands have always lived close to things that civilized peoples prefer to pretend do not exist, and the Shaman tradition emerged from that proximity over generations. Shamans serve their tribes as intermediaries between the living and whatever lies beyond — negotiating, appeasing, occasionally compelling. They regard the academic Binder traditions with open skepticism, having watched formally trained practitioners blunder into situations that any Shaman child would have known to avoid.

The Medium's relationship with the veil is the most permeable of any Binder tradition — less a practitioner who reaches through than one who allows things to reach back. Lorewise this means a willingness to let spirits temporarily inhabit and work through them, a practice that other Binder traditions find either impressive or horrifying depending on their temperament. The Medium walks a careful line between openness and dissolution, and not all of them maintain it indefinitely.

Where the Medium balances between forces, the Spiritualist leans entirely toward the creative side of the veil — the generative, the living, the light that exists beyond mortal perception. This sounds gentler than it is. The Spiritualist's pursuit of that creative force often pushes her to physical extremes, treating her own body as a secondary concern compared to what she is reaching toward. The results can be extraordinary. The cost is rarely small.

Among the exile communities and displaced peoples of the Abyssal Lands, the Animist tradition holds that every living thing carries a fragment of something beyond the veil — that the spirit world is not elsewhere but threaded through everything present. This is a less dramatic form of Binder practice than most, concerned less with summoning and more with listening. Animists tend to be patient people. The tradition selects for it.

The navigators of the Valis Confederacy read the stars to find their position on the sea, and the Astrologer tradition emerged from the discovery that the same stars that chart physical position also mark currents in the spirit realm. Valisian academies formalized this into a discipline — celestial observation as a form of veil-reading, omens extracted from the same sky that guides the fleet home. The Astrologer is among the most educated of Binder traditions and among the most comfortable with ambiguity, having learned that the stars rarely give simple answers.

The Zafeer people of Dynasia carry a tradition older than their current peace with the feudal throne — advisors trained to see what rulers cannot, drawing on veil knowledge to counsel, warn, and occasionally manipulate the powerful toward better decisions. The Vizier does not rule. The Vizier makes rulers worth following, or failing that, finds better ones. Dynasia absorbed the Zafeer tradition because it was too useful to suppress, and the Vizier has navigated that complicated institutional position with characteristic patience ever since.

Most Binders reach through the veil toward spirits, demons, entities that exist in relationship to humanity even if that relationship is predatory. The Alienist reaches further, toward presences that predate that relationship entirely — elder things, cosmic entities, beings for whom humanity is not an adversary or a resource but simply a fact of no particular significance. Hastur straddles the border between demon lord and elder presence, and Alienists who have contacted him rarely describe the experience in reassuring terms. The distinction between the Alienist and the Cultist is control — the Alienist refuses to serve. Whether the elder things notice this distinction is another question.

Every other Binder tradition involves some degree of asymmetry — the practitioner reaching toward something more powerful and managing that imbalance through skill, safeguards, or faith. The Pact Master has closed that gap. Through decades of accumulated power and understanding, the Pact Master negotiates with summoned entities as a genuine equal, offering terms rather than issuing commands or making supplications. Sandra Martin, who passed through the space between Heaven and Hell without training and survived, understands something about what lies beyond the veil that most Pact Masters spend lifetimes approaching. She arrived at that knowledge in an afternoon. It was not a pleasant afternoon.

Pack-commanding warrior who fights alongside a growing menagerie. He fuses the Barbarian's Anguish-driven aggression with the Binder's companion system, pushing his beasts harder as his rage builds — and hits hardest when his pack is largest.

Vulnerability-hunting hybrid who plants elemental weaknesses and detonates them with precision Seeker shots. He combines the Archer's aim economy with the Runemage's elemental attunement, making enemies progressively more fragile before landing attacks that punish specific weaknesses on critical hits.

Life drain as a resource. She attacks to drain, then spends that drain on enhanced attacks, purges, heals, and Spirit Power — with the Accumulated Blood capstone letting her bank drain across turns for explosive Blood Infusion payoffs.

Enchantment-fueled melee performer who fights better the more buffed she is. She generates expertise while enchanted, weaponizes her own buffs through sacrifice and exploitation, and brings the Bard's audience and song toolkit into the front line.

Meditative brawler who converts afflictions into weapons. He metabolizes debuffs by category — purging them to deal damage, gain mana, quicken, or strike back — while using influence and intangible states to control the battlefield from within it.

Healing-powered holy warrior whose offensive and defensive output both scale with how much he has been healed. The more his allies invest in him, the harder and more accurately he strikes — with mounted charge options, divinity-fueled domain effects, and the ability to die spectacularly and return.

Ammo-loaded elemental mage who banks mana for escalating power. The Esoteric suite rewards consecutive use by reserving mana and increasing output with each cast — building toward volatile releases that damage all enemies when the reservoir breaks, intentionally or not.

Shadow-cursing infiltrator who maledicts from hiding and exploits it from range. She cycles in and out of hidden to generate mana, weakens affliction resistance through poison, and plants malediction with melee attacks from cover before detonating it with dark magic.

A support specialist who weaponizes enchantments as both offense and defense. He stacks buffs on himself and allies, punishes enemies who strip them, and sacrifices his own enchantments for burst damage or emergency healing. His device funds protective shrine companions and warranty effects that shield enchantments from removal.

A tandem fighter who fights in concert with a spirit companion. He chains counters into companion quickens and damage bonuses, shapes his companion's element through his current form, and bridges alignment tools with the chakra ladder — Eros enhancing chance, Thanatos enhancing damage.

A dark melee specialist who combines challenge focus with permanent malediction. She layers hexes onto her challenge through dark slashes, spreads afflictions via contagion, and punishes enemies for attacking her by countering with additional curses.

A melee combatant who channels elemental magic through her blade. She builds expertise through elemental damage and mana use, enchants allies with elemental empowerments that transform her strikes into elemental follow-ups, and uses absorption moves to convert incoming elemental damage into mana and conflux charges.

A spirit-channeling earth fighter who pours anguish and runic power into totem companions. His totems shield allies, taunt enemies, and absorb punishment to generate more anguish, while his earth strikes hit hard and wide. Runic Rage lets him burn rune uses freely at the cost of losing them all when the wrath ends.

A precision attrition fighter who bleeds enemies out and finishes them with ruthless damage. He spends advantage on burst attacks and hidden-enabled backstabs, converts spirit power into poison shots and mass dark damage, and uses bleeds as setup — reducing the ruthless threshold so enemies already bleeding are always closer to an instant kill.

A divine marksman who locks onto a single target and prosecutes it with sustained trial abilities, generating aim through precision shooting and divinity through healing screens. He disenchants enemies, punishes corruption, and delivers justice-enhanced ranged strikes — with party-wide support benefits that persist as long as his focus holds.

A guardian who responds to ally suffering with psychic retribution. She builds influence over enemies while guarding a chosen ally, punishes enemy aggression with possession and judgment strikes, and has a full suite of reactions that fire when allies die — making every enemy kill a costly decision.

No faith owns the Oracle and no faith entirely trusts them. They exist at the intersection of all religious traditions as figures who have moved beyond institutional devotion into something that resembles a direct line to divinity itself — readers of Shaetavar's dreams who have stopped needing the interpretation the Preacher provides, visionaries whose pronouncements the Dynasian church cannot officially sanction and cannot afford to ignore. They are mythologized across all three Concord nations and regarded with the specific unease that genuinely holy things tend to produce in institutions built around managing holiness. They are rare, they are usually inconvenient, and they are almost always right.

Nobody is quite sure where Plague Doctors come from or who trained them, which is part of the problem. They appear in communities suffering from disease outbreaks, treat the sick with methods that blend religious ritual and genuine medicine, and move on before anyone can ask too many questions. The unaffiliated nature that makes them flexible and broadly deployable also makes them deeply suspect in a world already paranoid about cult activity. The accusation that they bring the diseases they claim to cure follows them everywhere. For the most part it is not true. The most part is doing a lot of work in that sentence.

The institutional backbone of the Dynasian church, the Priest occupies a formal role within the hierarchy — conducting ceremonies, administering sacraments, serving as the official face of Alister High's faith in a specific community or region. The distinction between the political and religious sides of the church manifests most visibly at the Priest level, where assignments are made and careers are managed by people whose motivations are not always purely spiritual. A Priest who serves their congregation well and a Priest who serves the church's political interests well are not always the same person.

The faith of Shaetavar the Sleeping God does not demand that its followers evangelize in the aggressive sense. The Preacher's role is gentler — to guide people toward right action, to interpret the subtle influence of the god's dreams on daily life, to maintain the faith as a living and breathing thing in communities across the Trader States. Some Preachers are genuinely devoted to this purpose. Others have noticed that a trusted religious figure occupies a position of considerable social influence, and have adjusted their priorities accordingly. Shaetavar, dreaming, may or may not be aware of the difference.

The Trinity of Marduk, Enlil, and Tammuz does not produce gentle faithful. The Valisian faith is a religion of the sea — of storms survived and enemies outrun and battles won through ferocity when seamanship was not enough — and the Zealot is its most extreme expression. In battle they function as something approaching clerical berserkers, their devotion translating directly into a frightening capacity for violence done in the name of their gods. The Grand Commodore values them as shock troops. The quieter members of the Valisian faith regard them with the complicated pride of people whose most famous representatives are also their most embarrassing ones.

Further along the Dynasian devotional path than the Acolyte, the Disciple has proven their commitment through years of service and begun to access more reliable and more powerful divine gifts. They are recognizable figures in Dynasian society — respected, trusted, occasionally envied. The political side of the church regards Disciples as a resource to be cultivated and directed. The religious side regards them as souls doing exactly what souls should do. The tension between those two perspectives is something every Disciple eventually has to navigate personally.

The church of Alister High has always maintained Exorcists, but for most of its history they were a minor specialty dealing with rare cases of possession and haunting. The weakening of the veil changed that overnight. The Abyssal Lands now host more spiritual corruption than the church has ever encountered, and Exorcists have flooded into the region in numbers that alarm the Binder traditions and deeply unsettle the Reapers. To the Exorcist, what the Reaper venerates and the Binder attempts to control is simply a problem to be solved. This perspective is not universally appreciated.

War produced the Combat Medic as a necessity and the peace has not eliminated them. Where the Healer serves a community, the Combat Medic serves a nation — embedded with military units, trained to work under conditions that would paralyze a sanctuary healer, devoted as much to the flag as to the faith. They come from all three Concord nations and their theological backgrounds vary considerably, united less by doctrine than by the particular psychology required to heal people while people are actively trying to kill them.

Outside the great cities and cathedral towns, the Healer is often the only representative of organized faith a farming community ever sees. They live among the people they serve — tending the sick, blessing the harvest, presiding over births and deaths — and their divine gifts are calibrated to exactly that scale of need. The church regards them as essential and somewhat unglamorous. The communities they serve regard them as indispensable. In the Abyssal Lands, where institutional presence is thin and suffering is not, traveling Healers are among the most quietly important people in the region.

The first step in the Dynasian church's long path of devotion, the Acolyte has accepted the faith of Alister High and begun the slow process of earning divine favor through service and study. The healing gifts that manifest in early training are modest and inconsistent — the church teaches that this is as it should be, that power proportional to devotion is the correct order of things. Most Acolytes spend years in this state before advancing. Some never do, and serve the church in other capacities. Father Martin began here, as everyone does.
“So, I speak the words, and the words are power, and power becomes reality.”
“Fire, earth, water, air? Inconsequential. All that matters is magic essence.”
“I shall burn away all resistance and dissent.”
“I am the fury of the storm incarnate. Behold me and prepare to be blown away.”
“I shall be seen as an equal by the demon lords.”
“A fingernail, some hair, a bit of blood. The resemblance is uncanny, isn’t it?”
“Too long has it been witches burned at the stake.”
“I didn’t understand what I would be giving up joining them.”
“It is so easy to underestimate the power of the written word.”
“You have become overly reliant on these spells of yours.”
“Leave me be, or you will regret it.”
“A simple answer for you: No.”
“You have no will of your own.”
“Time is just an illusion.”
“I knew what you were planning even before you did.”
“Look deep into my eyes…”
“Let me help you forget it all. Is there any greater gift I could give to you?”
“Don’t bother standing in my way. I have the power to move you.”
“I know what you’re thinking, and I would advise against it.”
Alpha's Mark — The Beastmaster's attacks deal increased damage for each companion currently present on the battlefield.
Indiscriminate Seeker — Elemental Seeker abilities can utilize any elemental vulnerability on the target, regardless of which element the Seeker ability specifies.
Accumulated Blood — Life drain abilities stack and are retained for the purposes of Blood Infusion abilities. This accumulated total resets when any Blood Infusion ability is used.
Unstrippable — The Bravo has a chance to parry disenchant effects.
Astral Discipline — While the Daevic is intangible, his attacks gain penetration and piercing.
Ally Restored — Allies being healed also enhances the Paladin's Restored value.

Esoteric Overflow — Whenever reserved mana is released by any means — voluntarily, through disruption, or by any ability that releases locked mana — the released amount deals damage to all enemies based on the total released. The Technomancer also has an increased chance to be disrupted while mana is reserved, balancing the power of accumulation against risk.
Shadow Mana — Whenever the Trickster loses the hidden condition, she gains mana based on the level of this skill.
Eldritch Swords — Sword abilities have a chance to trigger on an enchanted ally's attack, in addition to triggering through the Eldritch Warrior's own strikes.
Overwhelm Forsaken — Whenever the Enchanter targets an ally afflicted with forsaken with an enchantment ability, he has a chance to apply the enchantment despite the forsaken condition.
Companion Attack Counter — Whenever the companion is attacked, the Esoteric has a chance to counter on the companion's behalf.
Hexblade's Mark — Whenever an enemy dies from hex damage, a random other enemy is afflicted with that hex.
Trial Focus — The Inquisitor gains focus whenever he initiates a trial ability. This focus is lost when that trial ends.

Punishing Witness — Whenever an ally is struck by a critical hit, the Judge triggers a their ally death skill. Default effect: quickens the Judge. The triggered effect can be replaced through effect skills.
Totem Pole — Totem abilities stack with one another, building a single large companion that offers multiple combined buffs rather than replacing the previous totem.
Savage Findings — Enemies suffering from bleed have a reduced ruthless damage threshold against the Vivisectionist.
