Close In – Enhance allies' melee damage for next turn. Follows ranged attack (Ranger)
Distance Stance – Gains expertise when attacking back rows. Increases damage against back rows (Ranger)
Fan Out – Enhance allies' ranged damage for next turn. Follows melee attack (Ranger)
Melee Aim – Consume aim to enhance melee damage of next attack (Ranger)
Near Aim – Generate aim if aimed target is in front row (Ranger)
Persistence – Purge any provoke from non-aim targets and ignore any avert or scorn from aim target (Ranger)
Taunting Distance – Taunt enemy in back row and lower accuracy (Ranger)
Amplification Challenge – Initial Effect: High damage against target. Basic Effect: Gain amplification versus challenge. Challenge Effect: Use amplification against challenge (Shock Trooper)
Amplifying Blow – Melee attack with amplification that consumes ammo; also applies amplification to damage adds from ammo. Amplification resets on reload (Shock Trooper)
Blade Intensify – Air melee attack with amplification. Drains damage shield (Shock Trooper)
Buzzsaw Blow – Melee attack that causes bleed with penetration. Bleed type is based on current ammo (Shock Trooper)
Critical Intensify – Melee attack with high critical chance and damage. Drains damage shield (Shock Trooper)
Exact Shock Strike – Air elemental melee attack versus challenge (Shock Trooper)
Forcefield Assisted Strike – Melee attack with damage enhanced by damage shield on Shock Trooper (Shock Trooper)
Intensified Shot – Ranged attack that consumes ammo and damage shield. Additional effect based on current ammo type; see Intensified Shot ammo table under Teknixian (Shock Trooper)
Overcharge Forcefield – Doubles value of damage shield then deals damage based on damage shield value; disenchants damage shield (Shock Trooper)
Storm Intensify – Random air attacks based on amplification level. Drains damage shield and costs mana (Shock Trooper)
Tech Blade – Air melee attack with increased damage based on current air ammo. Requires air ammo (Shock Trooper)
Conductive Defense – If Shock Trooper would lose damage shield before her next turn, she deals air damage to all enemies (Shock Trooper)
Detonation Imbuement – Grants target a proc that has a chance to apply air damage detonations on attack (Shock Trooper)
Disjunction Response – Whenever damage shield is destroyed or disenchanted, Shock Trooper counters the enemy that caused this (Shock Trooper)
Forcefield Imbuement – Grants target a proc that increases damage shield on attack (Shock Trooper)
Forcefield Taunt – Taunt target enemy and gain damage shield equal to damage of next hit received, lasting for a standard duration (Shock Trooper)
Retaliate Intensify – Grants air retaliation to Shock Trooper with amplification. Drains damage shield (Shock Trooper)
Stun Intensify – Stuns all enemies based on amplification. Drains damage shield (Shock Trooper)
Barrier Prep – Gain barrier against next attack (Shock Trooper)
Forcefield Invigoration – Gain damage shield at the beginning of next turn based on air damage taken before next turn (Shock Trooper)
Gale Intensify – Delay all enemies. Drain damage shield (Shock Trooper)
Greater Intensify – Next Intensify ability drains more damage shield for a greater effect (Shock Trooper)
Provoke the Storms – Provoke all enemies; deal air damage to challenge when next damaged (Shock Trooper)
Reactive Forcefield – Gain damage shield that is lost after next time damaged (Shock Trooper)
Repulsive Forcefield – Stun and delay all enemies that attack before next turn. Requires damage shield (Shock Trooper)
Alignment Calling – Temporary companion based on alignment (Summoner)
Binding Trap – Next enemy to attack takes damage and is delayed and incapacitated (Summoner)
Carbuncle Call – Summons a carbuncle companion (Summoner)
Cyclops Calling – Earth magic attack versus all enemies that cannot be countered and benefits from companion passives. Requires no companion present (Summoner)
Dark Flock Rune – Element rune; magic dark damage and blind versus all (Summoner)
Dragon Calling – Fire magic attack versus all enemies that cannot be countered and benefits from companion passives. Requires no companion present (Summoner)
Mass Calling – Prepared; costs mana. Summons a temporary companion for each ally with an empty companion slot; all attack immediately then expire at end of turn (Summoner)
Phoenix Calling – Light magic attack versus all enemies that cannot be countered and benefits from companion passives; also heals team. Requires no companion present (Summoner)
Rune Calling – Temporary companion based on current power and damage runes (Summoner)
Rune Summons – Consumes one primed rune of each type (power, elemental, defense); summons a companion based on the combination (Summoner)
Summoned Doom – Untyped countdown that generates Thanatos on end (Summoner)
Treant Calling – Earth magic attack versus all enemies that cannot be countered and benefits from companion passives; also slows and delays all enemies. Requires no companion present (Summoner)
Tupilaq Minion – Summons a tupilaq companion. Tupilaqs gain greater effects from runes and procs (Summoner)
Acid Evolution – Companion gains additional earth damage with attacks; reserves mana (Summoner)
Eros Sigil – Next enemy to attack Summoner causes Eros gain and mana gain (Summoner)
Flanking Break – Companion attack against flanked enemy (Summoner)
Restorative Chain Rune – Heals master of any targeted companion whenever that companion attacks (Summoner)
Summoning Rune – Enchant rune that reduces mana cost and improves cast speed of summons (Summoner)
Thanatos Sigil – Next enemy to attack Summoner causes Thanatos gain and quicken cast (Summoner)
Towering Inferno Rune – Defense rune that causes fire damage to all enemies when hit (Summoner)
Alignment Binding – Moves alignment towards balanced to reduce cost of next summon (Summoner)
Lingering Portal – Follow summon with damage based on summon (Summoner)
Reaction Endowment – Companion counters any attack made against it or Summoner before its first turn (Summoner)
Rune Bestowal – Transfer runes from self to companion (Summoner)
Summoning Replacement – Greatly enhance summoning speed. Requires summon present (Summoner)
Stun Exploitation - The Thug uses multiple abilities that stun her enemies and multiple abilities that take advantage of that same stunned condition.
Armor Bash – Melee attack with clobbering that lowers target defense (Thug)
Berserk Backstab – Melee attack versus flanked enemy. Requires berserk (Thug)
Clobbering Advantage – Melee attack that consumes all advantage to deal increased clobber (Thug)
Clobbering Health – Clobbering melee attack that requires full health (Thug)
Critical Clobber – Melee attack with high clobber value on critical (Thug)
Disruptive Smash – Melee attack that disrupts stunned target (Thug)
Dogpile – Melee attack against flanked enemy. Deals additional damage based on ally timers then delays those allies (Thug)
Gang Rush – Melee attack against flanked enemy with attack from chosen allied unit (Thug)
Necksnapper – Melee attack against stunned target consuming advantage with massive damage (Thug)
Stun Clobberer – Melee attack against stunned target that deals clobbering damage (Thug)
Stunning Advantage – Melee attack against stunned that generates advantage (Thug)
Stunning Dispute – Attack, stun target and self, omega (Thug)
Stunning Thrashing – Melee attack that stuns target based on rage (Thug)
Unbalancing Smash – Melee attack that flanks enemy on critical (Thug)
Berserk Blindside – Melee attack against stunned target. Requires berserk (Thug)
Blindside Jab – Melee attack with delay against flanked target (Thug)
Push Past Exhaustion – Lower tired value. Requires rage (Thug)
Push Past Pain – Purge damage afflictions. Requires rage (Thug)
Tiring Poison – Afflict target enemy with poison that causes tired (Thug)
Endure Stuns – Chance to ignore stuns until next turn. Requires enduring (Thug)
Exhausting Advantage – Become tired to generate advantage (Thug)
Exhausting Strength – Become tired to enhance damage (Thug)
Flanking Shift – Cause flanking to stunned target (Thug)
Gang Up – If there are more heroes including companions than enemies, flank all enemies for one turn (Thug)
Stunning Rage – Generate rage for each stunned enemy (Thug)

Every cult has new members, and not all of them arrive knowing exactly what they have joined. The Cultist represents the earliest stage of demon lord service — drawn in by promises of power, belonging, or escape from circumstances that felt impossible to endure otherwise. Some discover the truth of their patron and embrace it. Some, like Kayla Edgars, discover it and find themselves unable to continue. The demon lords are patient with new recruits. They have learned that clarity about the arrangement tends to come later, when leaving is considerably more difficult.

Pazazu's servants carry the wind with them, a cold and howling presence that makes their allegiance difficult to mistake for anything benign. Warlocks are fully aware of what they have chosen and have chosen it deliberately, finding in Pazazu's domain a power that suits their particular temperament. The masculine associations the title carries in common usage are a misunderstanding the tradition itself does not share — Warlocks are defined by their compact with Pazazu, not by anything as incidental as gender.

Earth magic in service of a demon lord does not produce growth. The Dustbringer's tradition is associated with disintegration and a specific, creeping corruption that resists every attempt at purging — afflictions that settle into their targets and simply remain, indifferent to remedy. The earth theme here is entropy rather than foundation, the slow reduction of everything solid into something that blows away. Dustbringers tend to be patient practitioners. Their work rewards patience.

Mephisto and Moloch both claim fire, and the Effigist serves whichever of the two has claimed them, channeling infernal flame through effigy work that targets the representation of a person as much as the person themselves. The tradition has obvious dramatic power — burning an effigy carries cultural weight across most societies — and Effigists exploit that weight deliberately, understanding that fear of the symbolic act often precedes and amplifies the actual damage.

Nobody becomes a Hedgemage through ambition. They arrive at it through alienation — living on the outskirts of villages that want their folk cures but not their company, offering what help they can in exchange for an acceptance that never quite materializes. The power they access through their demon lord connection is real, even if they don't fully understand its source, and it serves genuine community purposes right up until the community disrespects them one time too many. The transformation from tolerated healer to vengeful practitioner rarely happens all at once. It accumulates.

Ipos leaves his mark in frost, and the Crone tradition carries that cold deep into its Russian-inflected folk practice — winter magic, ice and preservation, the specific cruelty of a cold that does not kill cleanly but preserves its victims in suffering. Crones exist at the intersection of old folk tradition and infernal service, their practice dressed in the clothing of grandmother wisdom while drawing on something considerably less benign. The aesthetic of the kindly old woman in the woods has always been ambivalent in the places where Crone tradition is strongest. It is more ambivalent now.

Where the Crone operates alone in her winter isolation, Hags gather. Three is traditional, though the number is flexible, and what they share is less a specific demon lord patron than a collective practice of malevolence — the weaving of fate, the cursing of the presumptuous, the specific satisfaction of power exercised without apology. They are among the most self-aware practitioners in the Witch tradition, under no illusions about what they serve or why, and find the self-deception of newer Cultists either amusing or contemptible depending on their mood.

The Mambo tradition sits close enough to Reaper spirit practice that outsiders frequently confuse the two, but the distinction matters to practitioners on both sides. Where Reapers approach spirits with something approaching respect, the Mambo's fetish bag work operates in service of demon lord power rather than the spirit hierarchy, using similar vocabulary for fundamentally different ends. Mambos exist most commonly in Valis and the Abyssal Lands, where the cultural proximity to genuine spirit worship provides both cover and occasional uncomfortable confrontation with Reapers who notice the difference.

The Bokor's zombies are not spirit-inhabited bodies and they are not the honored dead. They are enslaved — sometimes corpses, sometimes people who are technically still alive, rendered mindless and compliant through demon lord granted power that the Bokor deploys with complete indifference to the distinction. The Bokor does not care what their servants were before. They care only that they serve now. In the Abyssal Lands, where the war left bodies and broken people in abundance, the Bokor tradition has found more raw material than it has ever had before.

Every demon lord needs representatives in the mortal realm, and the Malefax has decided that representative should be them. Through forged covenants and accumulated power, the Malefax negotiates directly with demon lords for primacy among their cults — the right to speak with their patron's authority, to rule the networks of servants below them, to be the face of infernal power in the world. It is an arrangement that feels like elevation and functions like a leash. The demon lords have made these covenants before. They know exactly how much rope to extend and exactly when to pull it taut.

The generalist path through Wizard tradition, the Elementalist spreads their study across multiple elements without committing to the deep specialization their more focused peers pursue. This is sometimes a deliberate philosophical choice and sometimes simply an inability to choose, and the tradition does not particularly distinguish between these motivations. What it produces is breadth — practitioners who can adapt to whatever a situation requires, at the cost of the concentrated power that specialization provides. In a world as unpredictable as the post-war Abyssal Lands, breadth has genuine value.

Dark magic applied to life and death does not require demonic service, and the Necromancer tradition has always maintained that animating the dead is a neutral act rather than an evil one. Society has largely accepted this position, partly because Necromancers demonstrably don't serve demon lords and partly because after a war that produced as many dead as the last one, pragmatism about corpses has become more widespread. The only reliable source of offense is personal — the people who knew the skeleton companions in life, for whom the neutrality of the act is considerably harder to maintain.

Water magic attracts practitioners with a particular temperament — patient, adaptive, interested in flow and pressure rather than direct confrontation. Hydromancer traditions exist across all three Concord nations but flourish especially in Valis, where the element is immediately and constantly present and its properties are understood practically before they are understood magically. Valisian Hydromancers tend to have a sailor's relationship with water — respectful, unsentimental, aware of exactly how dangerous it can be.

Earth magic is the slowest and most enduring of the elemental disciplines, and Geomancers reflect that in their practice — methodical, heavily defensive, concerned with permanence in a way that more volatile elemental traditions find excessive. They are disproportionately common in the Trader States, where the guild system's appreciation for reliable infrastructure finds a natural resonance with magic that builds and holds rather than burns and moves.

Air magic is the most difficult elemental discipline to visualize and the most difficult to defend against, operating in the space between things rather than through direct force. Aeromancers tend toward an intellectual detachment that other elemental practitioners sometimes find frustrating — they are interested in the movement of things, in the spaces and pressures that govern how everything else behaves, which produces a distinctive combat style and a distinctive conversational style equally.

Fire finds practitioners in every nation and social context, partly because it requires less patience than earth or water and partly because its effects are immediately visible and dramatic in ways that attract a certain temperament. Pyromancer schools exist everywhere, producing the largest volume of Wizard graduates of any elemental specialty and consequently the widest range of quality. The Abyssal war found uses for Pyromancers on both sides, and their postwar reputation is complicated by how enthusiastically many of them participated.

The Arcanist's central conviction is that shaping raw magical energy into an element loses something essential in the process — that the purest and most powerful form of magic is arcana before it becomes anything specific. Where every other Wizard tradition treats elemental attunement as the goal, the Arcanist treats it as a compromise. This position is not popular in schools built around elemental curricula, and most Arcanists are either self-taught or trained by masters who found institutional magic too limiting. Mary Stanfield's wealthy, free-ranging education gave her exposure to this tradition among others, and its philosophical independence probably resonates with someone who has always had the resources to chart her own course.

Light magic is not moral magic, despite what its name implies and what practitioners in Dynasia's religiously inflected schools sometimes suggest. The Solomancer illuminates — literally and metaphorically, piercing defenses, exposing what is hidden, bringing things into clarity that preferred to remain obscure. In a world thick with cult activity and political deception, these are useful abilities that make Solomancers simultaneously valuable and unwelcome depending on whose secrets are being illuminated.

While most Wizards are concerned with what magic they can create, the Incanter is equally concerned with what magic they can stop. Channeling and counterspell work define the tradition — a deep familiarity with how other practitioners' magic operates, developed specifically to interrupt it. Incanters can recognize magical effects as they form and unmake them before they land, a defensive capability that makes them uniquely frustrating opponents for every other magic-using tradition. They are not popular at schools where the curriculum assumes magic is primarily something you do to others.

The pinnacle of Wizard practice belongs to those who have passed through elemental specialization and out the other side into genuine mastery of the full spectrum. Where the Elementalist spreads study without depth, the Thaumaturge has achieved depth in every element and learned to combine them in ways that individual specialists cannot approach. The most difficult magic of every element becomes available at this level — not through raw power but through comprehensive understanding, the accumulated wisdom of a practitioner who has refused to stop learning. Mary Stanfield, with her private tutors and elite schooling and the financial freedom to pursue knowledge wherever it leads, is perhaps better positioned than most to eventually walk this path.
Bear Cub – Summons a bear companion that gains increased damage and defense as it takes damage. (Beastmaster)
Berserk Command – The Beastmaster and her companion attack the same target simultaneously. Requires Berserk. (Beastmaster)

Bestial Transformation – Requires maximum Thanatos and a companion. Sacrifices the companion to enhance the Beastmaster based on the companion's stats. On use, makes an attack using the companion's attack with the Beastmaster's new stats. (Beastmaster)
Blood of Thanatos – Melee attack with backbiting, enhanced by Thanatos scale position. (Beastmaster)
Call Onslaught – Melee attack against a single target with damage based on the combined power of all present companions. Costs mana. (Beastmaster)
Call Stampede – Melee attack against all enemies with damage based on the combined power of all present companions. Costs mana. (Beastmaster)
Charge in Unison – Melee attack against the target from the Beastmaster and each other mounted unit. (Beastmaster)
Companion Charge – Melee attack versus a column with a damage bonus from the companion. Requires mounted. (Beastmaster)
Send Forth the Hound – The companion attacks the target, and the Beastmaster taunts that target. (Beastmaster)
Summon Riding Boar – Summons a boar mount. (Beastmaster)
Thanatos Mania – Melee attack enhanced by Thanatos scale position that inflicts Berserk on the Beastmaster. (Beastmaster)

Pack Commander — The Beastmaster coordinates a pack of companions alongside her own combat presence, with Anguish and Thanatos fueling the aggression of both herself and her beasts. Companion count and strength directly enhance several of her abilities.
Animal Friend – Heals the companion and enhances its defense based on the total number of companions present. (Beastmaster)
Bestial Intimidation – The companion taunts a target enemy and delays it. (Beastmaster)
Brutal Evolution – The companion's attacks gain backbiting. (Beastmaster)
Demands of Anguish – Quickens and enhances the damage of the companion based on current Anguish. (Beastmaster)
Rabid Beast – Possesses the companion to make an attack with enhanced damage and a chance to wound. Resets the companion's timer to 0. (Beastmaster)
Rising Temper – Enhances companion damage. Amplified. (Beastmaster)
Shared Wrath – The companion gains the benefits of the Beastmaster's active Wrath form. Anguish drains faster while active. Toggled. (Beastmaster)
Add to the Pack – Reduces the cast time and mana cost of the next summon based on the number of companions currently present. (Beastmaster)
Command Wrath – The Beastmaster enhances her companion while in this Wrath form. When this Wrath ends, the companion dies. (Beastmaster)
Immediate Assault – The next companion summoned by the target makes a free attack on arrival. (Beastmaster)
Kind Urging – Spend Eros to quicken the companion. (Beastmaster)
Mount Anything – Treat the Beastmaster as mounted until end of turn. Requires a companion. (Beastmaster)
Spur to Battle – Quickens the companion but deals it damage. (Beastmaster)
Spur to War – Quickens all companions but deals them damage. (Beastmaster)
Vulnerability Exploitation — The Blackthorn identifies and amplifies elemental vulnerabilities in enemies, then detonates them with precision ranged attacks.
Arrow Trap – Trap that triggers on the next enemy ranged attack. Causes three ranged pinpoint attacks. (Blackthorn)
Earth Seeker – Ranged earth attack that causes earth bleed. Requires earth vulnerability. Causes prone on critical. (Blackthorn)
Flame Seeker – Ranged fire attack that causes wound. Requires fire vulnerability. Deals fire damage to all enemies on critical. (Blackthorn)
Frost Seeker – Ranged water attack that delays the target. Requires water vulnerability. Incapacitates the target on critical. (Blackthorn)
Heart Seeker – Ranged attack dealing extra elemental damage based on the target's current vulnerability value. Requires any elemental vulnerability. (Blackthorn)
Lightning Seeker – Ranged air attack that quickens the Blackthorn. Requires air vulnerability. Attacks three random enemies on critical. (Blackthorn)
Manabane Blast – Delays and damages the mana of all enemies. (Blackthorn)
Manaburn Shot – Ranged attack with mana burn, enhanced by current aim. (Blackthorn)
Pinpoint Trap – Creates a ranged trap that deals pinpoint damage when the enemy with the lowest health makes an attack. (Blackthorn)
Resistance Snipe – Ranged attack that causes elemental resistance weakness on critical. (Blackthorn)

Shadow Vulnerability – Ranged attack that converts dark vulnerability to light vulnerability or light vulnerability to dark vulnerability. Requires one of the two vulnerabilities to be present. (Blackthorn)
Vulnerability Vow – Prepared air ranged attack that selects its target on preparation. Afflicts the target with air vulnerability on preparation. (Blackthorn)
Winged Arrow Rune – Elemental rune. Deals distant air damage to a single target. (Blackthorn)
Elemental Screen – Grants the Blackthorn a random elemental shielded and generates aim. Must be used as the last action of the turn. (Blackthorn)
Lightning Aim – Consumes aim to grant the Blackthorn an air damage add to the next attack. (Blackthorn)
Seeker Arrow – Afflicts the target with a random elemental vulnerability. Consumes aim. (Blackthorn)
Seeker Rune – Affliction rune. Afflicts the target with a random elemental vulnerability. (Blackthorn)
Vulnerability Interception – Prepared ranged air attack that activates when an enemy gains any elemental vulnerability. (Blackthorn)
Vulnerability Trap – The next enemy to use an elemental ability gains vulnerability to that element. (Blackthorn)
Empower Vulnerability – Increases the value of a vulnerability and refreshes its duration. (Blackthorn)
Floating Leaf Rune – Damage rune. Adds air damage to the attacks of the target. (Blackthorn)
Seize on Vulnerability – Prepared elemental damage attack against an enemy suffering from vulnerability. Alpha. (Blackthorn)
Vulnerability Transfer – Transfers an elemental vulnerability from the Blackthorn to the target enemy. (Blackthorn)
Watch for Vulnerability – Quickens the Blackthorn each time a vulnerable enemy is attacked before the Blackthorn's next turn. (Blackthorn)
Cover Vulnerability – Spots an enemy suffering from vulnerability to raise the related elemental resistance. (Blackthorn)

Blood Infusion — The Blood Blade converts life drained this turn into enhanced versions of her abilities. Blood Infusion abilities scale their effect or reduce their cost based on the total life drained since the Blood Blade's last turn.
Blood Challenge – Initial Effect: Pain link against target. Basic Effect: Backbiting attack. Challenge Effect: Increased backbiting attack. (Blood Blade)
Blood Feast – Melee attack with life drain. Deals enhanced damage based on the amount of life drained. (Blood Blade)
Blood Ripper – Melee attack that deals extra damage based on the number of bleeds on the target. (Blood Blade)
Bloodfire Blow – Melee attack with backbiting. Deals area damage based on the backbiting damage dealt. (Blood Blade)
Bloodlust Carnage – Melee attack against the challenge with bloodlust. (Blood Blade)
Bloodreap Strike – Melee attack that causes untyped bleed with reaping. (Blood Blade)
Bloodspikes – Melee attack and bleed versus the front row. (Blood Blade)
Call Blood – Deals heartstrike damage to a single bleeding enemy. (Blood Blade)
Decimation Drain – Melee attack with decimation and life drain. (Blood Blade)
Spirit Blood – Melee attack that causes bleeding based on Spirit Orbs held. Consumes Spirit Power. (Blood Blade)
Vampiric Strike – Melee attack with life drain. (Blood Blade)
Blood Infusion Hit – Attacks the challenge with a mana cost reduced by life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Blood Infusion Purge – Purges the Blood Blade with a mana cost reduced by life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Blood Infusion Spirit – Gains Spirit Power based on life drained this turn. Gains an extra Spirit Orb if the life drain killed. (Blood Blade)
Bloody Armor – Enhances defense with backbiting. (Blood Blade)
Bloody Weapon – Enhances damage with backbiting. (Blood Blade)
Bloody Imbuement – Grants the target an untyped bleed proc. (Blood Blade)
Vampiric Heal – Heals an ally based on life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Vampiric Spirit – While active, attacks gain life drain. Consumes Spirit Power over time. (Blood Blade)
Blood Infusion Cull – Culls an enemy with a mana cost reduced by life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Infusion of Defense – Enhances defense based on life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Infusion of Mana – Gains mana based on life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Infusion of Regeneration – Gains regeneration based on life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Infusion of Strength – Enhances damage based on life drained this turn. (Blood Blade)
Share Blood – Follows damage dealt to an enemy by spreading all bleeds currently on the Blood Blade to that target. (Blood Blade)
Lucky and Blessed - Attacks from the Bravo often either have the blessed modifier or require the lucky status, giving them higher chance to hit and higher average damage.
Aggressive Refrain – Possesses allied audience members to attack random enemies. (Bravo)
Blessed Blow – Melee attack with blessed accuracy. Grants lucky on critical. (Bravo)
Blessed Misfortune – Blessed melee attack against an enemy with unlucky. (Bravo)
Compelling Note – Melee attack that adds the target to the audience and compels them. (Bravo)
Condemned Blow – Melee attack with blessed accuracy that afflicts the target with unlucky on critical. (Bravo)
Enchanted Blow – Melee attack that deals increased damage for each enchantment on the Bravo. (Bravo)
Endangered Luck – Melee attack with blessed. Requires endangered. (Bravo)
Lucky Kill – Melee attack with culling. Requires lucky. (Bravo)
Self-made Fortune – Melee attack that consumes expertise for blessed damage and accuracy. (Bravo)
Spent Glory – Melee attack that sacrifices a random enchantment on the Bravo for increased damage. (Bravo)
Stripped Blow – Melee attack that disenchants the target first to deal additional damage. (Bravo)
Expert Enchanting – Enhances the enchant power of the target, increased by expertise. (Bravo)
Expert Luck – Grants lucky to the Bravo. Requires expertise. (Bravo)
Final Fortune – Lose lucky to make a melee attack with blessed attack and damage. (Bravo)
Forsaken Song – Reduces the purge chance of enemy audience members and causes enchantments on them to have a chance to fail. (Bravo)
Motivate with Kindness – Heals an ally and enhances their damage based on the amount healed. (Bravo)
Security Song – Enhances the block, parry, and dodge of audience members. (Bravo)
Song to Self – Heals the Bravo and adds her to the audience. (Bravo)
Enhancement Stance – Generates expertise at the beginning of every turn while enchanted. Enchantments used by and placed on the Bravo are more difficult to remove. Stance. (Bravo)
Enchantment Armaments – Prepared reaction. When the Bravo would take damage, sacrifice enchantments to reduce the damage taken. (Bravo)
Ideal Enchantment – If the Bravo is currently unenchanted, the next enchantment she gains has double duration. (Bravo)
Last Defense – Enhances parry chance. Requires endangered. (Bravo)
Naked Fury – Disenchants the Bravo of all enchantments to increase melee damage until end of turn, based on the number of enchantments removed. (Bravo)
Sacrifice Luck – Lose lucky to gain enduring. (Bravo)
Shared Bravado – Shares an enchantment currently on the Bravo with a target ally. (Bravo)
Consistent Growth — Consistency increases by a small amount at the start of each of the Avenger's turns.
Always Juggling — The Juggler begins battle already juggling. The level of this skill determines the starting juggle count.
Wide Splash — Splash abilities affect more enemies and have a greater effect.

Spell to Skill — The Magus gains stacks that improve her damage each time she switches between magic and melee attacks. The amount of stacks that can be gained is based on this skill level, and the stacks are lost when the Magus uses either two melee or two magic abilities consecutively.
Becoming Shadow — Whenever the Silhouette gains hidden, he has a chance to gain intangible as well.
Manavore — Draining mana also heals the Spelleater.
Drive Counters — While the Sybarite has a Drive ability active, she has greatly increased counter chance.
Sustaining Proc — Meta-proc. Can be attached to abilities used during the Warder's turn. When it activates, wards and other sustained abilities are sustained for free.

Unbroken Current — Whenever a channeled ability is disrupted, the Channeler generates mana based on how long it was channeled. This applies even to channeled abilities that already have their own disrupt effect.
Devil's Due — Damage dealt by the Diabolist is converted to corruption based on her own corruption level.
Wheel of Fortune — The Fortune Teller has a chance to change enchantments on enemies into related afflictions and afflictions on allies into related enchantments.
Blink State — The Nomad has increased spell dodge while intangible.
Flanking Stallion — Melee attacks made while mounted have a chance to flank the target before the attack takes place.
Chain Trigger — Whenever a hex triggers, there's a chance it triggers an additional hex on the same target.
Communal Pain — Whenever the Scourge takes damage from his own abilities, all allies gain a small amount of the same benefit that ability granted.
Returned Threat — Whenever the Warblade is attacked while provoking, he has a chance to taunt the attacker.
Past the Breaking Point — While exhausted, the Brawler is immune to being stunned, disarmed, incapacitated, or knocked prone.
Card Up the Sleeve — Whenever the Cartomancer uses a card trap ability, she causes an immediate draw against a random enemy. The number of draws scales with skill level.
Overflowing Tempo — Whenever the Conduit begins a channeled ability, she quickens all allies.
Reign of Fear — While the Frightmaster is present, frightened enemies have an increased base chance to cower instead of acting (base 85% instead of the standard 75%), scaling with skill level.
Final Justice — When the Justiciar is endangered, his justice value is increased, with the amount scaling based on skill level.
Vulture's Instinct — Whenever an ally is disenchanted, the Outlaw has an increased chance to critically hit with her next attack.

Relentless Pursuit — Whenever the Shadow's Following ability targets the same enemy as the previous turn's Following ability, critical chance increases. This increase stacks the longer the same target is followed.
Sacred Cycle — Whenever the Theurge uses a healing ability, her next magic attack deals more damage. Whenever she uses a magic attack, her next healing ability heals more.

A shapeshifting performer who copies whatever the battlefield produces. Her Mimic family reads field-wide actions from any unit and reproduces them instantly, Imitation Strike uses stolen enchantments to redirect enemy attacks onto the wrong target, and Enchanted Theft turns every charmed enemy's aggression into a personal wardrobe of stolen power.

A lone predator who hunts from between the physical and spectral worlds. He chains intangibility into hidden states and back again, exploits both conditions for devastating critical-focused attacks, and carries a spirit power economy that funds his most powerful strikes — including Strike Dead, the ultimate commitment to the kill.

A nature healer who prepares extensively before acting. The Poultice family covers nearly every support need in prepared form, vines and earth bleed handle battlefield control, and Natural Resilience turns every preparation window into a period of enhanced defensive fortitude — rewarding patience with survivability.

A berserk spellcaster who turns fury into firepower. She spreads berserk to enemies to make them attack her, refunds the cost of her most dangerous spells when berserk, and converts her anguish into piercing damage that cuts through whatever defenses remain standing after the fire.

A dual-wielding affliction specialist who punishes maledicted enemies from every angle. The Off-hand family turns every melee hit into a secondary effect, the expertise thread fuels both offense and affliction power, and Double Trigger makes landing both hits of a dual-wield strike the trigger for detonating every hex already sitting on the target.

A celestial tactician who maintains a constellation of active countdowns. Each Star ability buffs the whole party while its countdown ticks on an enemy, Stellar Bolt and Stellar Mana scale with the total number of active countdowns rewarding stacking multiple Stars simultaneously, and Stellar Magnitude makes every countdown last longer and hit harder.

A preparation-focused battlefield coordinator who stages multiple abilities simultaneously. Each prepared ability passively buffs the Tactician or an ally while waiting to fire, managing multiple preparations at once stacks those benefits, and Contingency Plan ensures that even a disrupted plan can be re-executed cheaper and faster on the very next turn.

A storm-riding mounted warrior who fills the battlefield with cascading air damage. She builds momentum for countdowns, chains storm attacks through the Reiteration family's delayed follow-up hits, and with Rolling Thunder every storm strike carries a chance to echo again as a weaker random hit — ensuring the storm never truly stops.
Apex Hunter - Whenever the Stalker attacks the enemy with the lowest current health, there is a chance he gains the hidden condition, allowing him to follow up with hidden-dependent abilities.
Early Harvest - The threshold at which enemies are considered endangered is raised passively, causing more enemies to qualify for poach triggers and endangered-targeting abilities sooner.
Windfall - Whenever an enemy that the Sharpshooter currently has a vow prepared against is killed by any means other than that vow being fired, the Sharpshooter is immediately quickened.
Infinite Draw - Whenever the Toxophilite activates an eternal ability, there is a chance the stack count increases by an extra point, compounding the power of eternal buffs beyond their normal rate.

Shared Sight – Grants an ally enhanced accuracy and pinpoint for their next attack. That attack must target the Archer’s current aim target. If the aim target is no longer available when the ally acts, the ally retains the accuracy and pinpoint bonus without the targeting restriction. (Archer)
Suppressing Fire – Lowers the accuracy of all enemies until the Archer’s next turn. Deals no damage. Does not reset aim. (Archer)

Hold Fire – Omega. Enhances the Archer’s next attack’s damage and accuracy. Can be used multiple times in succession, each use stacks the bonus further. Resets when the Archer makes an attack. (Archer)
Solo Hunter – Ranged attack. Requires the archer is alone. (Archer)

Shift Target – Transfers the Archer’s current aim to a new chosen target. The new target becomes the active aim target. Aim is transferred at 75% of its current value, with 25% lost in the transition. (Archer)
Exposed Flank – Applies the flanked condition to the current aim target. Requires aim. (Archer)
Bleeding Shot – Ranged attack that causes bleeding. (Reaper)
Bloodletting – Ranged attack that can only target bleeding enemies. (Reaper)
Carrion Field – Ongoing effect that deals damage to all enemies whenever any unit dies. (Reaper)
Culling Strike – Ranged attack with culling. Generates extra Spirit Orb on kill. (Reaper)
Decimation Arrow – Ranged attack with decimation. (Reaper)
Drain Shot – Ranged attack that drains life. (Reaper)
Fatigue Strike – Ranged attack whose damage scales directly with current Spirit Fugue level. (Reaper)
Gore Shower – Ranged attack that deals overkill damage to all enemies. (Reaper)
Grave Burst – Spend a large amount of Spirit Power, spiking Spirit Fugue, to unleash a damage burst against all enemies. (Reaper)
Greater Darkness – Blinds all enemies and lowers dark resistance. (Reaper)
Gushing Blood – Afflicts a target with hex based on the number of bleeds currently on it. (Reaper)
Death Surge – Spend a large amount of Spirit Power, spiking Spirit Fugue, to afflict all enemies with dark vulnerability. (Reaper)
Death's Edge – Reaping ranged attack with culling. Both reaping and culling trigger even on a miss. Only usable while in Spirit Fugue. (Reaper)
Basic Spirit Shot – Ranged attack that consumes Spirit Power. Requires two Spirit Orbs. (Reaper)
Reaping Shot – Ranged attack with reaping. Deals damage even on a miss. (Reaper)
Restore Spirit – Consumes Spirit Orbs to restore a single fallen ally to life at partial health. (Reaper)
Sanguine Tempest – Two-action ability. First action prepares it; second action releases, draining life from three random enemies and healing the Reaper. (Reaper)
Spirit Mending – Costs Spirit Power to heal a single ally. Increased effect while in Spirit Fugue. (Reaper)
Spirit Uprising – Resurrects all fallen allies at partial health. Very high Spirit Orb cost. (Reaper)
Thirsting Shot – Ranged attack with bloodlust, consuming Spirit. (Reaper)
Vampiric Reap – Ranged reaping attack with life drain. (Reaper)
Dark Gift – Grants an ally dark damage add for a period. (Reaper)
Fire Empowerment – Grants an ally fire empowerment. (Reaper)
Flame Gift – Grants an ally fire damage add for a period. (Reaper)
Mortal Fury – Enhances damage following any unit's death. (Reaper)
Mortal Shield – Enhances defense following any unit's death. (Reaper)
Soul Blight – Ongoing Spirit affliction against one enemy that causes corrupt bleed. Consumes Spirit Power. (Reaper)
Spectral Assurance – Ongoing buff that causes all of the Reaper's attacks to gain reaping. (Reaper)
Spirit Aura – Ongoing aura. Allies are healed whenever the Reaper drains life. (Reaper)
Spirit Tether – Targets a living ally. If that ally dies before their next turn, they automatically resurrect at partial health. No Spirit Orb cost. (Reaper)
Wretched Luck – Applies Unlucky to one enemy. Also applies Jinx while the Reaper is in Spirit Fugue. (Reaper)
Death Mana – Consumes Spirit Power to gain mana. (Reaper)
Feeble Spirits – Ongoing affliction against all enemies that reduces their damage. Consumes Spirit Power. (Reaper)
Hold Off – Close range delay. (Reaper)
Mortal Power – Generates mana following any unit's death. (Reaper)
Mystic Spirit Orbs – Consume a Spirit Orb to gain mana. More orbs possessed means more mana generated. (Reaper)
Retribution Ward – Buff on the Reaper or a single ally. The next attack against the target triggers a counter at standard counter damage. (Reaper)
Spirit Blessing – Ongoing buff on the Reaper or a single ally granting regeneration. Drains Spirit Power as upkeep. (Reaper)
Spirit Curse – Ongoing debuff on a single enemy sustaining the Cursed condition. Drains Spirit Power as upkeep. (Reaper)
Spirit Dissolution – Converts a Spirit Orb into Spirit Power. (Reaper)
Spirit Formation – Converts Spirit Power into a Spirit Orb. (Reaper)
Spirit Guard – Ongoing buff providing the Reaper with enduring. (Reaper)
Vengeful Revenant – Requires enduring. The next time enduring triggers, also gain enhanced damage on the next attack. (Reaper)
Blood Blister – Afflicts a target suffering from bleed with countdown based on the highest bleed value. (Buccaneer)
Chronic Symptoms – Afflicts a target suffering from countdown with hex based on the highest countdown value. (Buccaneer)
Constant Malignancy – Afflicts a target suffering from hex with bleed based on the highest hex value. (Buccaneer)
Deadly Expectations – Afflicts target with water countdown. If the sum of all countdown values exceeds half of the target's health, kills the target. (Buccaneer)
Drowning Sea – Field-based water bleed consuming Spirit Power over time. (Buccaneer)
Incoming Tide – Ranged attack that deals additional damage based on present hexes while reducing their duration. (Buccaneer)
Instant Blood Loss – Damages all enemies based on the duration and values of bleeds on them, then purges all bleeds. (Buccaneer)
Keelhaul – Ranged attack that consumes Spirit Power to deal water damage and bleed. If damage plus total bleed potential exceeds half of target health, kills the target. (Buccaneer)
Reaping Wave – Ranged water attack against the front row that deals reaping damage. (Buccaneer)
Swelling Wave Shot – Ranged water attack that afflicts the target with water hex. (Buccaneer)
Tide of Blood – Melee attack that deals additional damage based on the values of bleeds on the target. (Buccaneer)
Violent Swells – Ranged water storm with five attacks and reaping. (Buccaneer)
Walk the Plank – Ranged water attack that causes countdown. Spirit Power is generated when the countdown goes off. (Buccaneer)
Empathic Hex – Damages target based on the highest hex value on any enemy. (Buccaneer)
Massive Wave Reaction – Water attack versus all enemies following the Buccaneer taking massive damage. (Buccaneer)
Sea Gift – Grants a target ally water damage add for a period. (Buccaneer)
Suffer Restoration – Heals the Buccaneer for each enemy currently suffering from a damage affliction. Also generates Spirit Power. (Buccaneer)
Undertow Pull – Spirit aura that delays all enemies at the beginning of the Buccaneer's turn. (Buccaneer)
Water Empowerment – Grants an ally water empowerment. (Buccaneer)
Pass the Blame – Transfers all damage afflictions from a target enemy to a random enemy. (Buccaneer)
Personal Suffering – Increases the value of all damage afflictions on the Buccaneer. (Buccaneer)
Spirit Rime – Spirit aura that grants additional water damage add while draining Spirit Power. (Buccaneer)
Spiritual Regeneration – Drains Spirit Power and grants the Buccaneer regeneration. (Buccaneer)
Stable Footing – Prevents prone and flanked until the Buccaneer's next turn. (Buccaneer)
Watch for Death – Gain a Spirit Orb for any enemy that dies of a damage affliction before the Buccaneer's next turn. (Buccaneer)
Strike as One — Whenever any companion attacks, the General has a chance to immediately make a basic attack against the same target.
Misery Loves Company — Whenever the Hellion afflicts an enemy with a condition currently present on herself, that affliction has increased effect based on skill level.
Martyrdom — Whenever an ally would be killed by an attack, the Martyr takes increased damage from the attack instead.
Antagonistic Attacks — Attacks deal increased damage, but also deal damage to a random ally.
Change of Pace — Whenever Tempo resets, the Songblade gains quicken based on the stack count at the time of reset.

Spell and Arrow — Whenever the Spirit Guide scores a ranged critical hit, she makes a free magic attack. Whenever she scores a magic critical hit, she makes a free ranged attack. These free attacks cannot trigger this capstone.
Spell Poisons — Magic attacks can also apply poisons.
Domino Effect — Whenever a trap on the field triggers, there is a chance a second trap on the field also triggers immediately.

Hollow Remedy — Whenever an enemy heals, they take illusory damage based on a percentage of the amount healed for a short duration. If the target already has illusory damage, this duration merges with the existing condition, lasting for whichever duration is longer.
Perpetual Motion — Whenever the Dancer uses a dance ability, she gains quicken.
Dead Aim — The Deadeye has increased accuracy against frightened targets.
Resonant Burst — Whenever a detonation triggers, the companion is quickened.
Insanity Proc — The Mindblade has a chance to afflict the target with insanity with each melee strike. The chance scales with skill level.
Primal Fuel — Whenever the Primalist takes backbiting damage, she generates mana based on the damage taken.
Coiled Spring — Whenever a proc fails to trigger, its chance increases. This stacks until the proc triggers, at which point it resets to its normal value.
Mordant Response — The Warden has a chance to counter attack any disruption effect from an enemy, in addition to standard counter attacks.
Ancestral Fury — Whenever an ally dies, the Ancestral Blade's next attack is enhanced based on that ally's melee damage at the time of death.
Sacrificial Lamb — If an enemy would kill the Necrologist and she has a companion, the companion dies and the Necrologist suffers reduced damage instead.
Structural Collapse — Whenever the Sapper scores a critical hit against a fragile enemy, the fragile value on that enemy increases.
Final Chapter — Whenever the Scholar completes a scroll, she generates mana and her next magic attack deals enhanced damage.

Regenerative Vitality — Regeneration has a reduced effect on vitality, making its healing power resistant to diminishing returns. Standard heals have a greater effect on vitality, making them subject to faster diminishing returns.
Bewitching Illusion — Whenever the Spellweaver deals illusory damage to an enemy, that enemy has a chance to become charmed.
Combined Arms — Whenever the Weapon Master uses an ability with penetrate, clobbering, or shattering, the other two modifiers have increased effect until her next turn.
Feline Reflexes — Whenever the Wildcat would be struck by a critical hit, he has a chance to dodge it.

In the Line of Fire — Whenever any companion takes damage that would reduce it below a health threshold, the Arsenalist absorbs a portion of that damage instead. The amount absorbed scales with skill level.
Loss of Faith — Whenever the Blasphemer loses an enchantment, he generates mana and gains a stack of magic power enhancement.
Somnambulism — Whenever the Dreamstalker is incapacitated during her turn, she still makes an illusory attack against a random enemy.
Cascade of Ruin — Whenever an enemy triggers a trap, all hexes present on that enemy also trigger simultaneously.
Strong Throws — Ranged attacks gain a portion of all melee bonuses.
Automatic Sheathe — Whenever the Kensai makes an attack, she has a chance to sheathe her weapon afterward.
Against the Odds — The Liberator and all allies gain quicken based on current distress at the start of each of the Liberator's turns.
Djinni's Gift — The Sha'ir gains enhanced elemental power based on the element of her current companion.
Blind Fire — The Blind Archer is always blind. Whenever she misses with a ranged attack, she immediately repeats that attack against a random enemy.
Lingering Sigil — The effects of sigils last until the end of the previous target's next turn after transfer.
Undying Charge — Whenever the Ghost Rider or his mount receives a glancing blow, the mount is quickened.
Gathering Dusk — The dusk value for dusk abilities is increased by previous periods spent hidden, compounding across multiple hidden states.
Forking Jump — When an ability repeats, it has a chance to target two random enemies.
Entwined in Death — Companion deaths trigger the Mystic's own death skills, and the Mystic's death triggers companion death skills.
Second Fist — Whenever the Shifu uses an elemental fist ability, she has a chance to use a second, different elemental fist for free.

Raging Mercy — The Skald has increased healing and purge power while berserk. She also has increased healing and purge power when targeting berserk allies. These bonuses stack when both conditions are active simultaneously.
Enchanted Theft — Whenever a charmed enemy attacks an ally, the Chameleon gains a random enchantment from the charmed enemy.
Into the Mist — Whenever the Ghostfaced Killer gains intangible, he also gains hidden.
Natural Resilience — Whenever the Herbalist prepares an ability, he gains enhanced affliction and elemental resistance for a duration based on the time required to prepare it.
Piercing Madness — Attacks while berserk gain piercing.
Double Trigger — Whenever the Renegade hits the same unit with two attacks from one ability, she triggers any hexes present on the target.
Stellar Magnitude — All countdowns placed by the Stargazer have increased duration and increased power.
Contingency Plan — Whenever a prepared ability is disrupted, the Tactician can prepare that ability at reduced cost and with reduced preparation time on her next turn.
Rolling Thunder — Whenever a storm attack hits an enemy, there is a chance that hit reiterates after a period as a weaker random attack.
Enduring Grace: Heals incur a reduced vitality penalty, making subsequent heals more effective.
Measured Care: The Healer's heals incur a reduced vitality penalty, but the base vitality penalty from his heals is greater than standard.
Shattered Retribution: Whenever any ally's damage shield is destroyed, that ally immediately makes a free basic attack against the attacker.
Rest in Peace: Whenever a unit is healed while incapacitated, that heal does not affect vitality.
Purifying Fervor: Whenever the Zealot is purged of an affliction by any source, he is quickened. Each affliction removed counts separately.
Prophesied End: Whenever a countdown placed by the Oracle triggers on an enemy, that enemy takes increased damage from the next attack against them.
Festering Wounds: Whenever an enemy has three or more afflictions simultaneously, all affliction damage on that enemy deals increased damage. Applies to all sources.

Fractured Focus: While the Psychic is under half health, she gains a random piercing value between 0 and her missing health percentage at the start of each turn, lasting for the duration of that turn.

Camaraderie: Possession power is increased when possessing allies and decreased when possessing enemies, primarily affecting the damage dealt during possession and other possession power-based effects.
Assassination Hex – Hex that activates a cull on the target when it triggers. (Executioner)
Coward's End – Ranged attack that can only target the enemy with the lowest health. (Executioner)
Death Cascade – Ranged attack that repeats against a random target each time it kills. (Executioner)
Death Stroke – Ranged attack against an endangered and alone enemy. (Executioner)
Elemental Death Strike – If the target has an elemental weakness matching the Executioner's elemental empowerment, kills the target. (Executioner)
Eventual End – Ranged attack that causes a fire countdown. Can only target the enemy with the lowest health. (Executioner)
Exacting Executioner – Ranged attack with culling based on the value of pinpoint. (Executioner)
Executioner's Blow – Ranged attack that can only target a prone enemy. Increased critical damage. (Executioner)
Expanding Demise – Ranged attack against the enemy with the lowest health that deals overkill damage against the next enemy with the lowest health. (Executioner)
Grave Fire – Fire ranged attack that consumes Spirit Power. (Executioner)
Harvest Enchantments – Culls the enemy with the lowest health and gains its enchantments. (Executioner)
Harvest Mana – Culls the enemy with the lowest health and gains mana. (Executioner)
Hindering Umbrage – Ranged attack that delays enemies based on overkill. (Executioner)
Imminent Demise – Target takes damage based on life lost since this ability was prepared. (Executioner)
Ready the Final Blow – Prepared ranged attack that must target the enemy with the lowest health. Requires the enemy on preparation to be the same enemy on use. (Executioner)
Aura of Slaughter – Field-based effect that consumes Spirit Power to enhance the damage and bleeds of all allies and enemies. (Executioner)
Aura of the Endtimes – Spirit aura that increases the damage dealt to any endangered target. (Executioner)
Cinder Spirit – Activates a Spirit Orb and drains Spirit Power while causing fire damage to all enemies. (Executioner)
Dying Bloodloss – Afflicts an endangered target with untyped bleeding. (Executioner)
Specific Slaughter – Ranged attack against the enemy with the lowest health. (Executioner)
Culling Orb – Generates an extra Spirit Orb the next time the Executioner culls an enemy. (Executioner)
Fall of the Weak – Prepared ability that culls the enemy with the lowest health. (Executioner)
Mark for Death – The Executioner's next attack versus the target is culling. (Executioner)
Mystic Spirit – Drains Spirit Power to grant the Executioner increased mana generation. (Executioner)
Prepare the End – Enhances critical chance and damage until end of turn, but compels the Executioner to attack the enemy with the lowest health. (Executioner)

Bloodlust Finale – Ranged attack with bloodlust against the aim target. Consumes all aim, power scales with aim spent. After use, the Stalker’s aim is locked at zero for a duration scaled to aim spent. (Stalker)
Bloodlust Hunt – Ranged attack with bloodlust targeting enemy with lowest health. This eliminates aim if different target (Stalker)

Bloodlust Obsession – Ranged attack with bloodlust. This ability is locked onto the target until they die, he cannot use this ability against any other enemy. Area attacks remain available. If the target becomes untargetable, the Stalker must use other abilities until they can be reached again. (Stalker)
Bloodlust Seeker – Ranged attack with bloodlust and distance that consumes aim (Stalker)
Dark Fog Shot – Ranged attack and lower accuracy of all enemies until next turn (Stalker)

Excruciating Finale – Ranged attack with bleed against the aim target. Consumes all aim, power and bleed duration scale with aim spent. After use, the Stalker’s aim is locked at zero for a duration scaled to aim spent. (Stalker)
Hemorrhage Shot – Ranged attack that causes bleeding, consumes aim (Stalker)
Hidden Shot – High damage ranged attack that consumes aim and requires stalker to be hidden (Stalker)
Hidden Vow – Prepared ranged attack that selects target on preparation. Grants Stalker hidden on preparation (Stalker)

Impressive Finale – Ranged attack with enhanced critical chance and critical damage against the aim target. Consumes all aim, critical bonuses scale with aim spent. After use, the Stalker’s aim is locked at zero for a duration scaled to aim spent. (Stalker)

Incapacitating Obsession – Ranged attack that applies the incapacitated condition. This ability is locked onto the target until they die, he cannot use this ability against any other enemy. Area attacks remain available. If the target becomes untargetable, the Stalker must use other abilities until they can be reached again.

End the Hunt – Ranged attack against a chosen target. Transfers current aim to that target, making it the new aim target. Aim is transferred at full value. Intended as setup for a Finale against a new target. (Stalker)
Watching Darkness – Make a ranged attack against any enemy that attacks before next turn. Requires hidden (Stalker)
Camouflage Screen – Grants hidden and generates aim, must be used as last action (Stalker)
Femoral Bleed – Flank and slow target enemy suffering from bleed (Stalker)
Finale Aversion – Avert all enemies following using a finale ability (Stalker)
Finale Cull – Cull target enemy, but stalker cannot attack that enemy for a period after if it fails. (Stalker)
Perfect Beginning – Guaranteed hit with next attack against enemy at full health (Stalker)
Scent of Blood – Next attack gains bloodlust (Stalker)
Blood Blindness – Avert all bleeding enemies (Stalker)
Careless Aim – Reduce accuracy for next attack, raise aim, alpha (Stalker)
First Sight – Generate aim against target with no aim (Stalker)
Flanked Aim – Gain aim if target is flanked (Stalker)
Hiding Spot – Stalker gains hidden, consumes aim (Stalker)
Momentary Aim – Generates aim that is lost at end of turn. This cannot reduce aim below where it began (Stalker)
Protective Circuit: Whenever the Reliquarian places a detonation on an ally, that ally immediately receives a damage shield based on skill level. The shield does not stack with itself.
Siege Gang: Whenever any hero acts, the Machinist's active siege companion is quickened.
Sculpt Explosion: A percentage of friendly fire damage originating from the Bomber is reduced during the damage phase, applied directly to the ally damage calculation.

Personal Assistant: The Engineer begins battle with a self-targeted assistant that places a delay detonation on any enemy she attacks. Each attack places a separate detonation instance, which delays that enemy when the chain fires.

Adaptive Salvage: Whenever the Scavenger uses an elemental ability during her turn, her scavenged abilities replace their random element roll with that element for the remainder of the turn. Using a second element replaces the first.
Initial Accumulation: Accumulating abilities begin with an initial power value based on skill level rather than starting from zero.
Detonation Specialist: Whenever the Teknixian attacks an enemy, she deals increased damage based on the number of detonations currently on that target. All detonation types count equally.
Exploitation: whenever a negative proc triggers on an enemy, the Symbolist gains piercing for his next turn. Use it or lose it.
Festering: afflictions previously removed or purged from an enemy gain increased power when reapplied by the Hermit.
Siphon Enchantment: Whenever the associated proc triggers, lowers the potency of any enchantments on the target and increases the Disenchanter's disenchant power.
Trap Spotting: whenever a trap triggers, the Scrivener is quickened.

Elemental Cadence: Builds stacks on consecutive same-element abilities up to a skill-level cap, boosting damage of that element only. Hard reset on element switch or on acting after reaching max stacks.

Convergent Force: For each countdown the Sorcerer has active, his countdown power increases linearly. Affects base damage of Rising trio and base effect of Sustaining trio, but not the Rising doubling conditions.

Iron Preparation: Whenever a prepared ability that accumulates stacks while held is disrupted, a flat percentage of the accumulated stacks are retained rather than lost entirely. Applies to any class with stack-accumulating prepared abilities.

Residual Momentum – Whenever the Kinetic spends momentum, including accumulated momentum released from prepared abilities, she is quickened in direct proportion to the amount spent. Triggers on any expenditure regardless of size.
Ectoplasmic Goo – Arcane magic damage and slow versus single enemy. (Kinetic)
Energy Reversal – Channeled magic ability. Reduces damage taken while channeled, then deals damage equal to damage reduced to all enemies when the channel ends. (Kinetic)
Flame, Greater – Fire magic damage versus single enemy. (Kinetic)
Impaling Telekinesis – Telekinetic conversion attack with penetrate that causes untyped bleed. (Kinetic)

Kinetic Beam – Prepared telekinetic conversion attack versus a column. Accumulates momentum while prepared. On release, power scales with both the conversion mechanic and accumulated momentum. Accumulated momentum is not scaled again through the momentum tier system. (Kinetic)
Kinetic Blast – Telekinetic conversion attack versus all enemies. (Kinetic)
Kinetic Crush – Telekinetic conversion attack versus single enemy. Applies defense weakness and clobbering. (Kinetic)

Kinetic Delay – Prepared arcane magic attack versus all enemies. Accumulates momentum while prepared. On release, delay applied to targets scales with accumulated momentum. No telekinetic conversion. (Kinetic)
Kinetic Deterioration – Untyped magic bleed requiring momentum. (Kinetic)
Kinetic Storm – Fires 3 independently targeting magic attacks against random enemies. Each attack uses telekinetic conversion. Single mana cost. Triggers cast procs. (Kinetic)
Kinetic Wave – Telekinetic conversion attack versus all enemies. Enhanced by influence. (Kinetic)
Mindfire – Deal fire damage to all enemies enhanced by total influence. (Kinetic)
Momentum Bolt – Arcane magic attack requiring momentum. (Kinetic)
Enhance Momentum – Increases the momentum generated at the start of the Kinetic's next turn. (Kinetic)

Force Punch – Momentum-powered untyped physical attack. Requires a minimum of 15 accumulated momentum. Consumes only the minimum threshold — momentum above 15 remains after use. No telekinetic conversion. (Kinetic)
Kinetic Block – Prepared. Accumulates momentum while held. On release, grants the Kinetic a damage shield whose strength scales with accumulated momentum. (Kinetic)

Kinetic Momentum – Grants the Kinetic or a chosen ally a quicken and a damage add. Both scale with momentum consumed. Fully consumes all accumulated momentum on use. Can be used at low momentum for a weaker effect. (Kinetic)

Kinetic Shield – Reaction. When triggered, consumes accumulated momentum up to a maximum to reduce incoming damage by a percentage. If momentum remains after the reduction is applied, the reaction stays active. (Kinetic)
Kinetic Surge – Delays all enemies by a percentage of their current timer. Generates influence on enemies above 500 timer threshold. (Kinetic)
Chaos Elemental Wildsurge – Randomizes the element of all attacks used by the Kinetic and enhances their damage by a random amount, using Wild Surge mechanics. (Kinetic)
Draining Momentum – Delay all enemies based on momentum. (Kinetic)
Immediate Influence – Gain influence over enemy. Requires momentum. (Kinetic)
Mote of Anger – Positive. Enhances damage and quickens all allies on the Kinetic's turn based on total influence. (Kinetic)
Dampen Magic – Prepared. When released, reduces the magic power of the next magic attack used by enemies based on momentum accumulated while prepared. (Kinetic)
Telekinetic Grip – Delays enemy suffering from influence. (Kinetic)

Kinetic Conversion — Certain Kinetic abilities use telekinetic conversion. These abilities calculate initial damage using (magic power / magic resistance) x magic damage, then route the result through the physical damage path. Converted attacks are subject to dodge, block, counter, and parry, and cannot be countered by counterspells. They trigger cast procs rather than attack procs. All converted attacks deal physical damage.

Whenever a storm-classified ability would strike the Savant, including storm attacks redirected toward her by enemy abilities, there is a chance based on skill level to cancel that attack entirely before it resolves.

Faraday Shielding: Whenever a storm-classified ability would strike the Savant, including storm attacks redirected toward her by enemy abilities, there is a chance based on skill level to cancel that attack entirely before it resolves.

Finale Abilities — Finale abilities consume all of the Stalker's aim at once for a powerful effect, enhanced by the total aim spent. After using a Finale, the Stalker's aim is locked at zero for a duration that scales with the amount of aim consumed — more aim spent means a more powerful Finale but a longer recovery before aim can build again.
Amplified Influence – Generates influence on one target. Effect increases with each consecutive use. (Daevic)
Astral Dodge – Enhances dodge until the Daevic's next turn. Requires intangible. (Daevic)
Astral Majesty – Reduces damage dealt by any endangered enemy. (Daevic)
Cancel Corruption – Converts the next corrupt damage taken by the Daevic to regular damage. (Daevic)
Movement Metabolic Surge – Purges all movement afflictions from the Daevic and quickens him based on the number of afflictions purged. (Daevic)
Open to Affliction – Lowers the Daevic's own affliction resistance and enhances purge power. (Daevic)
Affliction Absorption – Heals the Daevic and grants mana when he is affected by afflictions. Requires leopard form. (Daevic)
Affliction Reflection – The Daevic has a chance for the next affliction targeting him to be reflected back to the attacking enemy. (Daevic)
Damage Metabolic Surge – Purges all damage afflictions from the Daevic and gains a damage add on the next attack based on the afflictions purged. (Daevic)
Mental Metabolic Surge – Purges all mental afflictions from the Daevic and gains mana and focus based on the afflictions purged. (Daevic)
Purity of Self – Heals the Daevic and grants mana. Requires being unafflicted. (Daevic)
Shadow Suspicion – Gains influence over all flanked enemies. (Daevic)
Stunning Influence – Stuns all enemies based on the influence held over each of them. (Daevic)
Amplified Illusion Punch – Melee attack that deals illusory damage. Effect increases with each consecutive use. (Daevic)
Astral Fist – Melee attack versus a stunned enemy that possesses it. (Daevic)
Elemental Metabolic Surge – Purges all elemental afflictions from the Daevic and deals related elemental damage to all enemies. (Daevic)
Exploit Anger – Melee attack against a berserk target. (Daevic)
Foresight Counters – Whenever an influenced enemy attacks before the Daevic's next turn, the Daevic counters it. (Daevic)

Intimidating Dragon – Melee attack that possesses the target to attack a random enemy. Requires dragon form. Lowers form on use. (Daevic)

Bury the Dead – Culls a buried target then removes the burial condition. (Gravedigger)
Earth Empowerment – Grants an ally earth empowerment. (Gravedigger)
Quaking Aura – Spirit aura that deals earth damage to all enemies at the beginning of the Gravedigger's turn. (Gravedigger)
Stone Gift – Grants an ally earth damage add for a period. (Gravedigger)
Tombstone Skin – Grants the Gravedigger a regenerating damage shield and fortify. Constantly drains Spirit Power. (Gravedigger)

Cough Up Blood – Damages all enemies suffering from tired. (Hangman)
Exhaustion Strike – Ranged attack enhanced by the tired value of the target. (Hangman)
Fugue Shot – Ranged attack requiring the Hangman to be in Spirit Fugue. (Hangman)

Restored Charge – Melee attack against a column. Requires mounted. Enhanced by Restored value. (Paladin)

Esoteric Chaos – Deals random elemental damage to all enemies. Reserves extra mana on each use but deals extra damage. Reserved mana is held until released or disrupted. (Technomancer)

Siphon Sleeper – Insidious mana drain against an incapacitated enemy. (Sandman)
Dark Dream Blast – Dark magic attack versus all enemies, enhanced by the number of incapacitated enemies. (Sandman)
Death in Sleep – Chance to kill an incapacitated enemy based on illusory damage present on it. (Sandman)
Dream Phantoms – Illusory damage versus all incapacitated enemies. (Sandman)

Sleep and Never Waken – Afflicts target with incapacitate and then culls if incapacitated. (Sandman)

Vampiric Whispers – Life drain following possession. (Whisperer)
Whispered Scream – Disrupts a target enemy suffering from distraction. (Whisperer)
Biting Whispers – Grants an ally untyped retaliation. (Whisperer)
Entrancing Apparitions – Consumes Spirit Power to stun all enemies. (Whisperer)
False Betrayal – Possesses a target enemy, but all damage is dealt as illusory. (Whisperer)

Sweet Nothings – Possesses and charms a target. (Whisperer)
Whispered Command – Dark magic attack that possesses the target. (Whisperer)
Whispering Paranoia – Ranged attack that consumes Spirit Power and deals additional damage based on the number of enemies adjacent to the target. (Whisperer)
Whispers of Control – Possesses a target enemy and afflicts it with dark hex. (Whisperer)

Bleeding Aura – Bleeds used have increased duration and potency. Drains Spirit Power over time. (Mercy Bringer)

Lonely Toxin – Spots a solo enemy to generate a poison use. (Mercy Bringer)

Ready for the End – Quickens on the next enemy death before the Mercy Bringer's next turn. (Mercy Bringer)
Dark Blood Poison – Applies dark bleed poison to attacks. (Mercy Bringer)

Frightful Awakening – Purges incapacitated from a target enemy and causes illusory damage. Generates Spirit Power. (Mercy Bringer)
Health in Adversity – Heals a target ally based on the number of enemies present. (Mercy Bringer)
Midnight Exposure – Afflicts a target enemy with dark exposure. (Mercy Bringer)
No Blessing – Disenchants a solo enemy. (Mercy Bringer)
Protracted Bloodloss – Refreshes all bleeds on a solo enemy. (Mercy Bringer)
Battle's End – Ranged attack with culling that can only be used if the enemy is alone. (Mercy Bringer)

Blood Shot – Ranged attack that deals maximized damage against a bleeding target. (Mercy Bringer)
Bloodthirsty Finisher – Ranged attack against a solo enemy with bloodlust. (Mercy Bringer)

Culmination of Torments – Chance to kill the target based on the number of afflictions on it. (Mercy Bringer)

Harvester's Wave – Ranged attack versus all enemies with culling and reaping. Generates extra Spirit. (Mercy Bringer)

Sudden Bloodloss – Ranged attack that purges all bleeds from a bleeding target, causing extra damage for each bleed purged, requires spirit fugue. (Mercy Bringer)

Atmosphere of Strength – The Gaslighter deals increased damage with all attacks. While not in Spirit Fugue, this drains Spirit Power over time. (Gaslighter)
