Atmosphere of Decay – All units take increased glancing damage. While the Gaslighter is in Spirit Fugue, glancing damage also causes defense weakness. (Gaslighter)
Atmosphere of Doubt – Enemies are delayed after they act. While the Gaslighter is in Spirit Fugue, they are also stunned. (Gaslighter)
Atmosphere of Terror – All units take increased illusory damage. While the Gaslighter is in Spirit Fugue, illusory damage does not expire or lose duration. (Gaslighter)
Disorienting Terror – All enemies take accuracy weakness based on their current illusory damage. (Gaslighter)
False Healing – The next time the target is healed, it takes illusory damage of the same amount. (Gaslighter)
Ghost Aura – Spirit aura. Intangible for all allies. (Gaslighter)
Shade Blows – Whenever the Gaslighter would deal a glancing blow, he deals full damage as illusory damage instead. (Gaslighter)
Delerium Smoke – Illusory air damage and stun versus all enemies. (Gaslighter)
Extermination Pulse – Spirit aura that culls any endangered enemy at the beginning of the Gaslighter's turn. Drains Spirit Power over time. (Gaslighter)
Gaslight Mist – Deals illusory damage to all enemies. Generates extra Spirit Orbs if illusory damage kills. (Gaslighter)
Greater Spirit Shot – Ranged attack that consumes Spirit Power. Requires three Spirit Orbs. (Gaslighter)
Heartfelt Fear – Ranged attack that deals illusory damage based on the target's max health. (Gaslighter)
Mind Games – Illusory damage versus all enemies and confuse based on Spirit Orbs. (Gaslighter)
Possessed by Terror – Possesses a frightened enemy, causing it to deal additional illusory damage. (Gaslighter)
Spirit Barrage – Dark ranged attack that makes one attack for each Spirit Orb. (Gaslighter)
Spirit Pyre – Magic fire attack against all enemies that delays and consumes Spirit Power. (Gaslighter)
Truth is a Lie – All enemies deal illusory damage instead of regular damage until the Gaslighter's next turn. (Gaslighter)
Spreading Terror – Deals illusory damage to all based on own illusory damage. (Gaslighter)
Cloak of the Arcane – Increase magic resistance. (Runemage)
Diamond Edge Rune – Adds an earth damage add to attacks of the target. (Runemage)

Elemental Resonance – Used on the same turn the Runemage uses an elemental ability. Grants enhanced power in that element until the end of the Runemage's next turn. Enhancement scales with the mana spent on the triggering elemental ability. (Runemage)

Elemental Warding – Used on the same turn the Runemage uses an elemental ability. Grants enhanced resistance to that element until the end of the Runemage's next turn. Enhancement scales with the mana spent on the triggering elemental ability. (Runemage)
Lightning Rune – Attacks of the target quicken self. (Runemage)
Prime Runes – Provides a charge boost to all prepared runes. Reduces disruption chance on rune abilities. (Runemage)
Runic Focus – Drains a set amount of charge from the power rune to gain quicken and focus. (Runemage)

Spell Stymie – Field trap. Single use. When an enemy activates the trap, lowers that enemy's magic power for the duration of their current turn only. Has no effect if triggered by a non-magic-using enemy. Situationally powerful in magic-heavy encounters. (Runemage)
Stonespike Armor Rune – Defense rune; target deals earth retaliation damage when attacked. (Runemage)
Earth Shudder Rune – Timing rune that delays all enemies when it triggers. (Runemage)
Bonfire Rune – Damage rune; attacks of the target deal fire damage to all enemies. (Runemage)

Elemental Opening – Follow-up move action. Can only be used after the Runemage has used an elemental attack this turn. Applies the related elemental vulnerability to one chosen target of that attack. For single-target attacks the target is automatic. For multi-target elemental attacks, the Runemage selects which target receives the vulnerability. (Runemage)
Explosive Barrier – Grants an ally a barrier. If the unit would take damage exceeding the barrier, the attacker is damaged. (Runemage)
Frost Frailty Rune – Timing rune; water-element countdown that causes brittle on expiry. Can be consumed for its expiration effect. (Runemage)
Mana Capture Trap – Field trap; when any unit spends mana, the Runemage recovers 25% of that mana. Arms after the Runemage's turn. (Runemage)
Mystic Warding – Enhance team magic resistance. Can be sustained without costing mana. (Runemage)

Sorcerous Barrier – Grants the Runemage a single-use damage barrier until the start of his next turn. If the barrier absorbs an attack before expiring, generates a flat amount of mana. If untriggered, the barrier expires at the start of the Runemage's next turn with no mana generation. (Runemage)
Structural Defense – Unit trap on a target ally; when that ally is critically hit, they gain fortification for a period after the attack. (Runemage)
Structural Weakness Rune – Reaction rune on target; causes defense weakness. If the target takes a critical hit, they become fragile. (Runemage)
Whirlwind Rune – Defense rune; target becomes quickened and gains enhanced dodge when attacked. (Runemage)
Basic Runespell – Magic attack that combines a primed power rune and a primed elemental rune for an effect. (Runemage)
Crackling Cloud Rune – Air elemental rune; four randomly targeting air magic attacks. (Runemage)
Cycling Countdown – Afflict target with an elemental countdown, changing element with each use. (Runemage)
Cycling Hex – Afflict target with an elemental hex, changing element with each use. (Runemage)
Exhausted Power Rune – Power rune; magic attack that drains mana from the target. (Runemage)
Flametrap Rune – Reaction rune; when the targeted unit acts, all enemies take fire damage. (Runemage)
Frostbind Rune – Water elemental rune; magic attack that causes slow. (Runemage)
Infused Power Rune – Power rune; magic attack that enhances the user's magic power. (Runemage)
Mystic Minefield – Field trap with multiple uses; fires arcane damage whenever any enemy uses an attack action. (Runemage)
Recharging Fire Rune – Timing rune; fire damage engine that recharges on activation while mana allows. Can be consumed for its expiration effect. (Runemage)
Recharging Lightning Rune – Timing rune; air damage engine that recharges on activation while mana allows. Can be consumed for its expiration effect. (Runemage)
Remnant of Autumn – Air damage versus column with delay; grants Runemage air damage add for a period. (Runemage)
Remnant of Spring – Earth damage hex versus target; grants Runemage earth damage add for a period. (Runemage)
Remnant of Summer – Fire damage bleed versus all; grants Runemage fire damage add for a period. (Runemage)
Remnant of Winter – Water damage versus row with disrupt; grants Runemage water damage add for a period. (Runemage)
Runic Amplification – Sacrifice a random rune to deal damage to target; amplification. (Runemage)
Stalactite Rune – Reaction rune; when the targeted unit acts, it is attacked by piercing earth damage. (Runemage)
Stonefall Rune – Earth elemental rune; magic attack that causes delay. (Runemage)

Surge Bolt – Prepared single-target untyped magic attack. Generates a flat amount of mana on use instead of consuming it. Damage is intentionally low — this ability exists to sustain the Runemage through the accumulation phase while runes charge. Does not contribute to Elemental Cadence stacking. (Runemage)

Surge Blast – Prepared untyped magic attack against all enemies. Generates a flat amount of mana on use instead of consuming it. Damage is intentionally low — this ability exists to sustain the Runemage through the accumulation phase while runes charge. Does not contribute to Elemental Cadence stacking. (Runemage)
Crow Rune – Defense rune; target deals dark damage when attacked. (Abjurer)
Dispersion Abjuration – The next proc from the target's defense rune affects all enemies at reduced potency. (Abjurer)
Double Retaliation – The next time the target is attacked, retaliation deals double damage and is then lost. (Abjurer)
Fortifying Grasp – Fortify target ally and delay them. (Abjurer)
Prime Defense Rune – Pushes a defense rune toward the primed state. (Abjurer)
Abjuration Shielding – Requires a primed defense rune; provides a target ally with an elemental shielded based on the current rune. (Abjurer)
Circle of Protection – Grant all allies fortification. (Abjurer)
Crashing Wave Rune – Defense rune; attackers become slowed when they attack the bearer. (Abjurer)
Earth Shielding – Grant target ally earth shielded. (Abjurer)
Steel Shield Rune – Enchantment rune; grants a damage shield that refreshes at the beginning of each turn until exhaustion, at which point it is removed. (Abjurer)
Stonewall Rune – Defense rune; target gains a stack of fortification each time it is attacked. (Abjurer)
Summoned Shield – Grants a block chance and block amount until the Abjurer's next turn. (Abjurer)
Abjuration Blast – Low accuracy magic earth attack against all; grants Abjurer a damage shield based on number of enemies hit. (Abjurer)
Acidic Armor Blast – Magic earth attack that also grants the Abjurer earth retaliation. (Abjurer)
Antimagic Field – Disenchants, disrupts, and damages the mana of all enemies. (Abjurer)
Boulder Fall – Earth magic attack versus a single random enemy. (Abjurer)
Earth Balance – Afflict target with earth vulnerability and gain earth shielded. (Abjurer)
Earth Shield Explosion – Magic earth attack against all enemies. Requires and consumes the Abjurer's own damage shield. (Abjurer)
Forcefield Crush – Arcane magic damage versus an enemy that has a damage shield; damage scales with the shield's value. Phasing. (Abjurer)
Halo Rune – Elemental rune; causes light magic damage to target and grants the Abjurer a barrier. (Abjurer)
Protection Runespell – Combines a primed power rune and a primed defense rune for an effect. (Abjurer)
Stone Hex – Afflict target enemy with earth hex. (Abjurer)
Unstable Pillar – Unit trap on the Abjurer; when the Abjurer is attacked, deals earth damage to all enemies. (Abjurer)
Warding Pulse Rune – Timing rune; on expiry grants all allies a short-term barrier. Can be consumed to deal arcane damage instead. (Abjurer)
Enforced Intercession – Redirect the next attack against the Abjurer to an ally. Functions better when a defense rune is active on that ally. (Abjurer)
Momentary Curse – Curses the target until the end of its next turn. (Symbolist)
Proc Call, Allied – Trigger a positive defensive proc on a target ally. (Symbolist)
Proc Call, Opposed – Trigger a negative defensive proc on a target enemy. (Symbolist)
Torch Rune – Adds a fire damage add to the attacks of the target. (Symbolist)
Trigger Detonation – Detonation that triggers hex, contagion, and negative defense procs on the target. (Symbolist)
Bloodjar Rune – Reaction rune; heals the Symbolist when an enemy dies. (Symbolist)
Countdown Detonation – Afflict target with a countdown that activates all detonations on the target when it triggers. (Symbolist)
Dull Edge Trap – Unit trap; the target enemy's next attack deals half damage (blunted). (Symbolist)
Independent Trigger – Trigger an attack proc against a target enemy without attacking. (Symbolist)
Mana Boon Trap – Trap that generates mana for the Symbolist when activated. (Symbolist)
Scar Rune – Reaction rune; damage afflictions caused by the target deal additional damage on use. (Symbolist)
Burn – Fire bleed against a single target. (Symbolist)
Chaos Wall – Deals random elemental damage to an enemy row. (Symbolist)
Dragon Fire Rune – Elemental rune; magic fire damage and bleed versus all enemies. (Symbolist)
Explosive Detonation – Detonation that deals fire damage to all enemies. (Symbolist)
Fire Balance – Afflict target with fire exposure and gain fire empowerment. (Symbolist)
Fire Reiteration Rune – Reaction rune; deals fire damage to target. Fire attacks against target deal fire damage to all enemies. (Symbolist)
Flame Wall – Fire magic attack against an enemy row that causes fire bleed. (Symbolist)
Pandemonium Detonation – Detonation that deals chaos damage to all enemies. (Symbolist)

Triple Flame – Three sequential fire magic attacks against a single target. First can proc enhanced fire on the Symbolist. Second can proc fire weakness on the target. Third can proc a fire countdown. Order matters. (Symbolist)

Clay Golem – Summons a clay golem companion. Dismisses any current companion. (Cabalist)
Dekastone – Magic earth attack versus a single target. (Cabalist)
Earth Reiteration Rune – Reaction rune; next earth attacks against the target also cause earth bleed. (Cabalist)
Earthworks Rune -Elemental rune; earth magic damage to a single target and fortifies the Cabalist. (Cabalist)

Solitary Mana – Gain mana if alone (last ally standing). (Hermit)

r.t: — The Archer's foundational resource, built as a percentage that climbs toward a maximum cap through the act of pressing an attack home. Once at hand, it can be spent — consumed by abilities for a bonus that scales directly with the amount put in. Everything else the Archer does is a question of how that percentage gets earned and where it gets spent.

— Aim is a relationship with one enemy, not a general resource. It only builds through repeated attacks on the same target, and switching targets erases it entirely — a real cost for retargeting, not a formality. Area and random attacks are the sole exception, passing through untouched by the reset, which keeps AoE options from being a trap for anyone managing aim on a priority target.

— Aim's most universal payoff is passive: the more of it an Archer holds against the current target, the more likely their attacks are to land. Beyond that baseline, many abilities key their own power directly to current aim, so the same ability grows more dangerous the longer the Archer has stayed locked onto one enemy — turning patience into a compounding advantage rather than a flat bonus.

— Vows are prepared ranged attacks that lock their target the moment they're readied, then wait — held indefinitely until the Archer chooses to loose them. Each Vow carries two distinct effects: one that fires immediately on preparation, and one that fires only when it's finally used. The risk is entirely borne by the target: if it dies before the Vow is called in, the preparation — and the action spent on it — is wasted.

— Every ranged attack in the game carries a reload delay, pushing the attacker back on the clock after firing. No class lives inside that rule the way the Archer does — ranged damage is the entire premise of the kit, not one option among several, so the delay isn't an occasional inconvenience but the standing tax the class pays for the privilege of hitting anyone, anywhere, from turn one.

— The Barbarian's foundational resource, generated by the act of taking damage itself — from enemies, from self-inflicted Backbiting costs, or from deliberate self-harm — regardless of how much health remains when the damage lands. It has two parts: a spendable pool and a ceiling that rises as damage accumulates over time. Spending Anguish draws down the pool but never the ceiling, so using abilities never weakens a future Wrath — it only spends what's available right now. Slot passives can unlock a single secondary generation channel (critical hits, enemy spellcasting), but only one such channel can be active at a time.

— The Barbarian's active power state, entered as a minor action, during which the Anguish pool refills toward the ceiling each turn. Every Wrath form pairs its benefit with a mirrored consequence — a damage boost ends in exhaustion, a resistance boost ends in vulnerability — and the pool's drain accelerates the longer Wrath continues, eventually outpacing generation and forcing an end. End Wrath lets the Barbarian exit early, conserving remaining Anguish and shortening the mirrored consequence that follows — rewarding a Barbarian who reads the fight rather than riding the drain to its limit.

— A condition that trades targeting control for damage. Each attack made while Berserk rolls for bonus damage, and the higher that roll climbs, the greater the chance the attack redirects to a random unit on the field instead of the intended target — at the extreme, even an ally. Berserk gates a portion of the Barbarian's kit outright: some abilities require it to function, others modify how it behaves, making the choice to enter or avoid Berserk a real fork in how a turn plays out, not just a damage modifier layered on top.

— Abilities that deal self-damage as part of their cost or effect, making that damage simultaneously a price paid and a resource earned — because Anguish generates from the act of taking damage, Backbiting abilities fund the Barbarian's own Wrath even as they cost her health. Their primary effects stand on their own merit; the Anguish they generate is a bonus for choosing pain, not the reason to choose it. This duality — power drawn directly from self-inflicted harm — is the Barbarian's defining thesis rather than an incidental side effect.

— A minor-action defensive preparation that grants immunity to one debuff category and a resistance bonus to one associated element. Only one Warpaint can be active at a time, and applying a new one replaces whatever came before. Its value is matchup-dependent — powerful against the enemy it counters, close to irrelevant against one it doesn't — but Painted Weapon converts the active Warpaint's defensive value into an offensive bonus on the next attack, giving it a reason to exist even when its defensive half will never trigger.

si.t: Prime Damage Rune – Pushes a damage rune toward the primed state. (Glyphic)

r.t: — The membership system underlying the entire Song mechanic. A unit enters the audience through a note ability and remains for a duration that must be refreshed through reapplication. Audience membership and the durations of individual chords or dischords are tracked separately — a chord or dischord can expire and stop affecting everyone while the audience itself persists, or a unit can leave the audience while an unrelated chord keeps running for whoever remains. A skilled Bard is juggling both clocks at once, not just one.

— The delivery method for Audience membership. Flats are applied to allies and carry positive effects; sharps are applied to enemies and carry negative ones. Using either does double duty: it both applies its own effect and brings the target into the audience (or refreshes them if already present), making these the entry point through which every other song pillar becomes possible.

— The actual content of the song: chords are persistent buffs affecting every ally in the audience, dischords are persistent debuffs affecting every enemy in it. The Bard can hold a limited number of each — starting at three, expandable to six through skills, seven total at maximum — and exceeding that limit replaces the oldest one first. This is the pillar that defines what the song is actually doing to the battlefield at any given moment.

— The audience-wide payoff ability type. A refrain triggers an effect against every member of the audience simultaneously — allied or enemy, depending on the refrain — and refreshes the song in the process, but at real cost. This is the highest-impact, most expensive pillar in the family, rewarding a Bard who has built up a full audience and song before cashing in.

— Every Bard subclass carries an unusually deep investment in enhancements and enchantments — the abilities, passives, and capstones that apply, extend, or amplify positive conditions run stronger and more frequently here than in almost any other class's kit. This isn't confined to the Song system itself; it shows up in dedicated stat lines, subclass-defining mechanics, and capstone skills built entirely around making buffs land harder and last longer. (Reflection abilities — turning a specific incoming attack back on its source — tend to surface later in this same vein, once a subclass has already leaned into the broader pattern.)

— The Binder's positional resource, a nine-step track running from Eros Full through Balanced to Thanatos Full, moved only when an ability explicitly shifts it. The scale governs access rather than expenditure: pushing toward one side makes the opposite resource progressively harder to generate — unaffected at the 1/4 mark, halved at 1/2, cut off entirely at 3/4, and actively draining at Full. Many abilities require a specific scale position to use at all, independent of whether the Binder can afford their cost, making position itself a gate the Binder must navigate rather than just a side effect of spending.

— Eros and Thanatos exist as two independent spendable resources, generated primarily through dedicated attacks and shift abilities, and consumed to pay for anything that requires them. Eros abilities skew defensive and restorative; Thanatos abilities skew aggressive and corrupting. Crucially, the pools and the scale move independently — spending from a pool doesn't touch scale position, and moving the scale doesn't touch pool values unless an ability's cost explicitly ties the two together.

— The payoff for reaching a scale extreme: Celestial Transformation and Infernal Transformation are major abilities gated behind maximum Eros or maximum Thanatos respectively, each dealing damage to all enemies while granting the Binder a lasting self-buff — regeneration and a light damage add on the Eros side, retaliation and a dark damage add on the Thanatos side. They exist as the concrete reward for committing fully to one direction rather than hovering near balance.

— Summoning is the Binder's central identity; she is built as the most capable summoner among the original sixteen classes, with a roster of light-aligned, dark-aligned, and unaligned creatures gated behind the appropriate Eros or Thanatos requirement. A companion, once summoned, acts as its own unit on the field, and the Binder's kit is built around supporting, empowering, and coordinating with whatever she's brought into the fight.

— Two distinct ways the Binder invests in a companion beyond the initial summon. Evolutions are permanent upgrades that grant a companion new defensive or offensive capabilities for the rest of the battle. Endowments are one-time boosts applied to whichever companion is summoned next, spending their effect the moment that summon occurs. Together they let the Binder treat her companions as something to be shaped and reinforced over the course of a fight, not just summoned once and left alone.

si.t: Accelerated Schedule – Reduce the timer for each countdown present on the target. (Cryptic)
Deadman's Switch – Prepared ability; triggers any countdown abilities present on the next enemy to die. (Cryptic)
Forge Rune – Defense rune; target deals fire damage when attacked. (Cryptic)
Mana Echoes Rune – Timing rune; increases mana generation while active. Can be consumed for an immediate mana burst. (Cryptic)
Watch for Fate – Quicken for each countdown that triggers before the Cryptic's next turn. (Cryptic)
Brittle Reverberations – Lower the resistance of any countdown present on the target. Untyped countdowns lower defense instead. (Cryptic)
Echoing Tremors – Timing rune; delay and disrupt countdown that repeats targeting the enemy with the most prepared abilities if mana allows. (Cryptic)
Ether Gap – Trap affliction that increases the chance for the target to take critical hits. Causes extra earth damage and disappears on critical. (Cryptic)
Life Blossoms Rune – Timing rune; countdown heals the ally with the lowest health each time it triggers. Recasts while mana charge allows. Can be consumed for immediate effect. (Cryptic)
Redirection Rune – Enchantment rune; causes next attacks against the bearer to grant a damage add of the same type. Associated with pain link. (Cryptic)
Repeating Remedy – Timing rune; countdown purge that recasts on each expiry while mana allows, targeting a random ally. Can be consumed for its expiration effect. (Cryptic)
Amplifying Countdown – Long duration countdown that increases in damage for each other countdown that triggers while it is present. Enhanced with amplification. (Cryptic)
Borrow from Fate – Magic attack that deals additional damage based on countdowns present on the target. Damage element matches the most powerful countdown on the enemy. (Cryptic)
Brittle Echoes – Earth countdown that lowers all elemental resistances of the target while present. (Cryptic)
Echoes of Destruction – Water magic attack and water countdown that repeats on each critical hit. (Cryptic)
Echoing Explosion – Timing rune; fire countdown versus all enemies that recasts on each expiry while mana allows. Can be consumed for its expiration effect. (Cryptic)
Entropic Power Rune – Power rune; magic attack with high damage range and bleed. Increases damage range and adds bleed to attached spells. (Cryptic)

Fate's Edge Rune – Timing rune; countdown that increases in power each turn it remains active. Consumed for a chaos magic attack against all, scaled to how long it ran. Natural expiry deals lesser damage. (Cryptic)
Prismatic Countdown – Causes an elemental countdown of each element against a random target. (Cryptic)
Prismatic Echoes – Afflicts target with fire countdown, repeating against a random target on trigger for each element in sequence. (Cryptic)
Recharging Frost Rune – Timing rune; water damage engine that recharges on activation while mana allows. Can be consumed for its expiration effect. (Cryptic)
Resonance Blast – Air countdown; deals air damage to all enemies if the target dies from this or any source before the countdown fires. (Cryptic)
Resonance Bolt – Air countdown; deals air magic damage to a random enemy if the target dies from this or any source before the countdown fires. (Cryptic)
Spreading Flames Rune – Elemental rune; deals fire magic damage to all enemies. (Cryptic)
Triple Darkness – Three sequential dark magic attacks: first with cull, second with corrupt, third with dark hex. (Cryptic)
Careful Weaving – The Sorcerer's next spell has increased cast time and reduced mana cost. (Sorcerer)
Prime Power Rune – Pushes a power rune toward the primed state. (Sorcerer)
Devoted Resistance – Prepared ability; reserves mana and enhances mana resistance. (Sorcerer)
Runic Infusion – Generate mana based on the number of runes currently prepared. (Sorcerer)
Sustaining Health – Personal countdown targeting only the Sorcerer; provides ongoing health regeneration while active. (Sorcerer)
Sustaining Mana – Personal countdown targeting only the Sorcerer; provides ongoing mana generation while active. (Sorcerer)

Barrier Dome Rune – Enchantment rune; provides a barrier to the entire team for the next several attacks that exceed a damage threshold. If a single attack triggers the barrier for multiple allies, only one use is consumed. (Sorcerer)
Bright Mind Rune – Defense rune; the bearer gains focus when attacked. (Sorcerer)
Leyline Flares – Countdown that increases mana generation for all units while active. Mana spent to place it is refunded on expiry. (Sorcerer)
Mana Siphon, Opposed – Gain a portion of the mana used by a target enemy. (Sorcerer)
Mystic Acceleration – Countdown that increases cast speed of all spells while active. Mana spent to place it is refunded on expiry. (Sorcerer)
Unweave Magic – Disenchant and disrupt a target enemy. (Sorcerer)
Absolute Power Rune – Power rune; magic attack versus all enemies. Enhances the magic power of all units currently in play. (Sorcerer)
Delayed Explosion – Magic fire attack versus all enemies. Can be sustained to increase damage. (Sorcerer)
Delayed Storm – Major ability that can be delayed to add additional strikes and increased damage. (Sorcerer)
Demonic Grin Rune – Elemental rune; untyped decimate damage versus the front row. (Sorcerer)
Diabolic Power Rune – Power rune; dark magic attack versus a single target with corrupt damage and frighten. Grants abilities corrupt damage. (Sorcerer)
Eldritch Power Rune – Power rune; arcane magic attack versus all with illusory damage that can cull enemies. Grants abilities illusory damage. (Sorcerer)
Eldritch Unraveling – Magic attack with culling that restores mana on kill. (Sorcerer)
Growing Bolts Rune – Elemental rune; magic air damage versus a single target with cascade. (Sorcerer)
Power Runespell – Combines a primed power rune, a primed affliction rune, and a primed enchantment rune for a powerful effect. Requires three different primed rune types. (Sorcerer)
Rising Crag – Earth countdown versus an enemy row. Doubles in power if Rising Stalagmite is active on the same target. (Sorcerer)
Rising Earth – Earth countdown versus all enemies. Doubles in power for each of Rising Crag or Rising Stalagmite currently active. (Sorcerer)
Rising Stalagmite – Earth countdown versus a single enemy. Enables the Rising synergy chain. (Sorcerer)
Sustaining Power – Personal countdown targeting only the Sorcerer; provides ongoing magic power enhancement while active. (Sorcerer)

Elemental Stance – Stance that increases elemental damage. The Eldritch Warrior generates expertise based on the amount of elemental damage dealt. Advanced: Increases elemental penetration effects. (Eldritch Warrior)
Empowering Speed – Quicken a target ally with empowerment. (Eldritch Warrior)
Empowerment Critical – If the next action deals elemental damage and scores a critical hit, gain the elemental empowerment corresponding to that element. (Eldritch Warrior)
Fleeting Defense – Enhance the Eldritch Warrior's own elemental defense based on the target's current empowerment, lasting until the target's next turn. (Eldritch Warrior)
Fleeting Element – The Eldritch Warrior's next melee attack gains an elemental damage proc matching the target's current empowerment. (Eldritch Warrior)
Lasting Empowerment – Extend the duration of any empowerment on the target. Also extends any active Sword ability tied to that empowerment. (Eldritch Warrior)
Mana Stance – Stance that increases mana generation. The Eldritch Warrior generates expertise when using mana. (Eldritch Warrior)
Air Absorption – Until the Eldritch Warrior's next turn, reduce incoming air damage. When targeted by an air ability, gain mana and charge air. (Eldritch Warrior)

Conflux Fighting – The Eldritch Warrior gains an ongoing buff that causes her attacks and criticals to also deal additional arcane damage as a proc. Lasts until replaced. Requires at least 3 elements charged. (Eldritch Warrior)
Earth Absorption – Until the Eldritch Warrior's next turn, reduce incoming earth damage. When targeted by an earth ability, gain mana and charge earth. (Eldritch Warrior)
Expert Magic – Enhance the magic power of the target. This enhancement is increased by expertise if the user is a fighter. (Eldritch Warrior)
Fire Absorption – Until the Eldritch Warrior's next turn, reduce incoming fire damage. When targeted by a fire ability, gain mana and charge fire. (Eldritch Warrior)
Water Absorption – Until the Eldritch Warrior's next turn, reduce incoming water damage. When targeted by a water ability, gain mana and charge water. (Eldritch Warrior)
Arcane Slash – Melee attack that also deals additional arcane damage. (Eldritch Warrior)
Doublecast Cantrip – Magic attack that fires a fire magic strike followed immediately by a water magic strike. Requires fire and water attunements. (Eldritch Warrior)
Expert Acidslash – Earth melee attack that grants an earth damage add. Requires expertise. (Eldritch Warrior)
Expert Fireslash – Fire melee attack that grants a fire damage add. Requires expertise. (Eldritch Warrior)
Expert Frostslash – Water melee attack that grants a water damage add. Requires expertise. (Eldritch Warrior)
Expert Shockslash – Air melee attack that grants an air damage add. Requires expertise. (Eldritch Warrior)

Sword of Dark Temptation – Enchant an ally with dark empowerment. While an ally bears this enchantment, this ability becomes Strike of Dark Temptation: a dark melee attack that provokes an enemy to attack the enchanted ally. (Eldritch Warrior)

Sword of Flaming Wrath – Enchant an ally with fire empowerment. While an ally bears this enchantment, this ability becomes Strike of Flaming Wrath: a fire melee attack that grants the enchanted ally fire retaliation. (Eldritch Warrior)

Sword of Fortifying Earth – Enchant an ally with earth empowerment. While an ally bears this enchantment, this ability becomes Strike of Fortifying Earth: an earth melee attack that grants the enchanted ally fortification. (Eldritch Warrior)

Sword of Lightning Calling – Enchant an ally with air empowerment. While an ally bears this enchantment, this ability becomes Strike of Lightning Calling: an air melee attack that grants the enchanted ally haste. (Eldritch Warrior)

Sword of Liquid Form – Enchant an ally with water empowerment. While an ally bears this enchantment, this ability becomes Strike of Liquid Form: a water melee attack that grants the enchanted ally intangible. (Eldritch Warrior)

Sword of Radiant Protection – Enchant an ally with light empowerment. While an ally bears this enchantment, this ability becomes Strike of Radiant Protection: a light melee attack that averts an enemy from attacking the enchanted ally. (Eldritch Warrior)
Enchantment Contagion – Shares a random enchantment currently on the Enchanter with all allies. Requires the contagion condition. (Enchanter)
Enchantment Warranty – Spends one ammo to prevent the next disenchantment effect against the target ally. (Enchanter)
Forsaken Purge – Purges the forsaken condition from a single target ally. (Enchanter)
Guarded Enchantments – All allies gain increased disenchant resistance until the Enchanter's next turn. (Enchanter)
Inherit Enchantments – When a target ally dies, the Enchanter gains all enchantments that were present on that ally at the time of death. (Enchanter)
Sacrifice Enchantment – A target ally loses one random enchantment and is healed for a value based on the enchantment sacrificed. (Enchanter)
Barrier Upgrade – Spends one ammo to grant a barrier to the target ally. (Enchanter)

Enchantment Heal – Sacrifices all enchantments currently on the Enchanter to heal and purge all allies. The power of the heal and purge scales with the total value of enchantments consumed. (Enchanter)

Enchantment Trap – Places an enchantment trap on a target ally. When the trap expires naturally, it heals the target. If the trap is removed for any reason other than duration expiration, it deals water damage to all enemies instead. (Enchanter)
Expiring Song – Dischord that causes enchantments on enemies in the audience to expire at twice the normal rate. (Enchanter)
Mana Countdown – Enchants a target ally with a countdown that restores mana when it activates. (Enchanter)
Refresh Enchantments – Refreshes the remaining duration of each enchantment currently on the target. (Enchanter)
Song of Enchantment – Chord that grants increased enchantment potency, power, and duration to allied audience members. (Enchanter)

Battle Shrine – Consumes all ammo to summon a companion that grants offensive enchantments to allies each turn. Power and duration scale with ammo consumed. Standard companion rules apply. (Enchanter)
Disenchantment Vengeance – Ranged attack with damage based on the number of enchantments disenchanted from any unit since the Enchanter's last turn. (Enchanter)
Echoing Note – Ranged note that adds the target to the audience and afflicts it with an untyped countdown. (Enchanter)
Enchanted Shot – Ranged attack that requires the Enchanter to be enchanted. Power scales with the number of enchantments currently on the Enchanter. (Enchanter)
Enchantment Blast – Disenchants all enchantments currently on the Enchanter and deals magic damage to all enemies based on the total value of enchantments consumed. (Enchanter)
Enchantment Proliferation – Copies all enchantments currently on a single ally to all other allies. (Enchanter)
Enchantment Storm – Water magic storm attack that makes one strike per enchantment currently present on the Enchanter. (Enchanter)
Frost Bolt – Single target water magic attack. (Enchanter)

Protection Shrine – Consumes all ammo to summon a companion that grants defensive enchantments to allies each turn. Power and duration scale with ammo consumed. Standard companion rules apply. (Enchanter)
Resonant Refrain – Refrain that afflicts all enemies in the audience with an untyped countdown. (Enchanter)
Spare Enchantment – The Enchanter loses a random enchantment currently on himself to deal damage to a single enemy. (Enchanter)
Tidal Crescendo Refrain – Refrain that afflicts all enemies in the audience with a water countdown. (Enchanter)
Balance Counter – Instead of countering the next attack, the Esoteric gains focus and is quickened. (Esoteric)
Compelling Advice – Following the Esoteric's next counter, compels the target of that counter to attack the companion. (Esoteric)
Dual Counter – The Esoteric's next counter also triggers a simultaneous counter from the companion. Delays both the Esoteric and the companion. (Esoteric)
Enlightened by Revenge – Following the Esoteric's next counter, he restores mana. (Esoteric)
Focus Command – Sacrifices the Esoteric's focus to command the companion to make an attack. (Esoteric)
Ghostly Companion – Grants the companion intangible for a period. (Esoteric)
Assumption of Balance – Enhances the Esoteric's defense. If the Esoteric is hit before his next turn, he assumes monkey form. (Esoteric)
Coordinated Counter – The Esoteric's next counter also quickens the companion and enhances its damage. (Esoteric)
Ephemeral Being – Prepared ability. Grants all allies intangible. Requires Thanatos alignment. Costs mana. (Esoteric)
Form Evolution – Grants the companion a damage type based on the Esoteric's current form. (Esoteric)
Mana Response – Restores mana to both the Esoteric and the companion when the Esoteric counters. (Esoteric)
Monkey's Trick – Requires monkey form. If the Esoteric is currently hidden, he gains intangible at the beginning of his turn. If he is not hidden, he gains hidden instead. (Esoteric)
Ancestral Kami – Summons a kami companion. (Esoteric)
Branching Lotus – Melee attack against the target and one random additional enemy. Flanks both targets. (Esoteric)
Crane Evades Attack – Melee attack that enhances dodge. Requires crane form and lowers form on use. If the Esoteric dodges before his next turn, he returns to crane form. (Esoteric)
Cynosure Fist – Melee attack against the target. If the target attacks the Esoteric before his next turn, the Esoteric is guaranteed to counter. Requires focus. (Esoteric)

Dragon Roar – Melee attack requiring dragon form. On use, the Esoteric arms an automatic counter, if triggered, it deals damage and stuns all enemies, with both effects scaling with the number of open chakras. Raises form to mantis if the counter fires; lowers form to monkey if no counter occurs. (Esoteric)
From the Ether – The Esoteric and his companion each make a powerful attack against the target enemy simultaneously. Requires and removes intangible from the companion. (Esoteric)
Heart of Battle – Melee attack that enhances critical chance and counter chance if Eros-aligned, or critical damage and counter damage if Thanatos-aligned. (Esoteric)

Karmic Strike – Prepared reaction. When the Esoteric is next attacked, he counters with bonus damage based on how much damage the triggering attack dealt. If that attack would have killed him, the counter damage is further increased. Consumes enduring. (Esoteric)
Lotus Bloom – Melee attack with decimate. Requires the Esoteric to be intangible. On a miss, the Esoteric loses intangible. (Esoteric)
Mana Punisher – Prepared melee attack that generates mana on hit. On a critical hit, inhibits the mana of all opponents and deals additional damage based on the mana they lose. (Esoteric)
Mirror Counter – Prepared reaction. When the Esoteric is next attacked, he counters and summons a mirror image companion that lasts for a short period. (Esoteric)

Serpent Seeks Revenge – Melee attack that causes earth bleed and damage weakness. Requires snake form and raises form on use. If the Esoteric counters before his next turn, he returns to snake form. (Esoteric)
Tandem Strike – Melee attack made immediately following the companion being attacked. (Esoteric)
Concentration Taunt – Taunts all enemies and the Hexblade cannot be disrupted until her next turn. Delays the Hexblade. (Hexblade)
Hex Aegis – If a hexed enemy attacks the Hexblade before her next turn, that enemy triggers its hex an additional time. (Hexblade)
Hexwatch – If an enemy dies from hex damage before the Hexblade’s next turn, she gains mana and enhanced affliction power. (Hexblade)
Insidious Nightmare – Triggers all hexes and contagion on an incapacitated enemy with the insidious modifier. (Hexblade)
Susceptible Challenge – The challenge gains affliction resistance weakness until the end of the turn. (Hexblade)
Provocation Hex – Triggers the hex on a target enemy and taunts it to attack the Hexblade. (Hexblade)
Challenge Reflex – Dark magic attack against the challenge. (Hexblade)
Challenge Sympathy – The challenge gains a random affliction currently affecting the Hexblade. (Hexblade)
Death Empowers – Follows killing an enemy. The Hexblade gains a dark damage add to attacks for a period. (Hexblade)
Hex Counter – The Hexblade’s next counter is replaced with applying a dark hex to the attacker instead of making a physical counter. (Hexblade)
Hex Imbuement – Grants a target ally a proc that applies a dark hex with their attacks. (Hexblade)
Malediction Reflex – Melee attack against the maledicted target. (Hexblade)
Provoke Malediction – Provokes all enemies currently suffering from malediction to attack the Hexblade. (Hexblade)
Contagion Call – Melee attack that spreads a random affliction from the target to adjacent enemies and causes contagion on the target. (Hexblade)
Curse Challenge – Initial Effect: Afflicts target with a dark hex. Basic Effect: Triggers the hex on the challenge. Challenge Effect: Amplifies and extends the hex on the target. (Hexblade)
Dark Sleep – Melee attack against a maledicted target that incapacitates it. (Hexblade)
Draining Challenge – Initial Effect: Establishes a heal siphon against the target. Basic Effect: Melee attack with a chance to proc drain. Challenge Effect: Melee attack with drain. (Hexblade)
Exposing Slash – Melee attack that procs dark exposure on the target. (Hexblade)

Heavy Dark Slash – Prepared melee attack with a powerful dark damage add. Deals increased damage if the target is the challenge, maledicted, or both — each condition applies and stacks independently. (Hexblade)
Malefaction Strike – Melee attack that causes malediction on the target. (Hexblade)
Malefactor’s Corruption – Melee attack against a maledicted target that causes corruption. (Hexblade)
Malignant Slash – Melee attack that weakens the target’s dark resistance and affliction resistance. (Hexblade)
Nihilistic Spread – Melee attack against a corrupted enemy. On kill, afflicts all remaining enemies with corruption. (Hexblade)
Spreading Slumber – Incapacitates the challenge target, then triggers all hexes and contagion on it with the insidious modifier. (Hexblade)
Stolen Hex Slash – Melee attack that grants the Hexblade a proc on her next attack causing it to spread one of the target’s current afflictions to adjacent enemies. (Hexblade)

r.t: — The Cleric's foundational resource, earned by fulfilling the role of healer and protector rather than by dealing damage. Any ability tagged as a heal, enchantment, purge, or resurrection generates divinity when prepared, whether it targets the Cleric himself or an ally; offensive and control abilities never generate it, regardless of secondary effects. Generation scales modestly with scope — a group heal produces more than a single-target one, though never enough that one cast fills the resource alone — meaning the Cleric must sustain his support role across the whole battle to accumulate anything meaningful.

— A large share of divinity-spending abilities draw on the entire pool at once, with their power scaling directly to the total amount spent — though this isn't universal, and a meaningful minority of divinity-consuming abilities work differently, spending only part of the pool or requiring a threshold without spending anything at all. For the abilities that do follow the full-consume pattern, the central decision is timing: reading the battlefield and choosing the right moment to cash in everything that's been built, rather than trickling divinity out in small amounts.

— Minor-action team buffs that interact with divinity in both directions: using one generates divinity and grants a modest benefit to every ally. Repeating the same prayer amplifies both its effect and its mana cost with each successive use, and both the bonus and the cost decay over subsequent turns if the Cleric moves his attention elsewhere. This creates a real choice between rotating prayers to keep everything affordable and providing steady value, or committing to one prayer for an escalating payoff at escalating expense.

— Ongoing minor-action effects that persist as long as the Cleric maintains enough divinity to sustain them, draining a small amount each turn. Only one domain can be active at a time, and each opens an additional, theme-specific divinity generation path that supplements rather than replaces the standard heal/enchant/purge/resurrection model — rewarding a Cleric who builds his tactics around his chosen domain's identity. Switching domains costs a minor action and a small amount of divinity, trading flexibility against competing for that same action economy.

— Every unit in the game is subject to Vitality: healing grows less effective the more of it a target has already received, with a floor that can be approached but never reduced to zero effectiveness. No class lives inside this rule the way the Cleric does — healing is the entire premise of the kit, not a supporting tool, so Vitality isn't an occasional inconvenience but the standing tax the class pays for being the game's primary source of sustained health recovery.

si.t: Aimed Disenchantment – Disenchants the target, consuming aim based on the value of the enchantment removed. (Inquisitor)
Current Focus – Gains focus if a trial ability is currently active. (Inquisitor)

Inquisition Domain – Reduces the duration of enemy enchantments at the beginning of each of the Inquisitor’s turns. Requires a minimum divinity to activate and consumes divinity each turn. Remains active as long as divinity stays above the minimum threshold. While active, generates divinity based on the pinpoint value or excess accuracy of the Inquisitor’s attacks. (Inquisitor)
Marked by Divinity – Consumes one divinity to lower the target’s dodge and defense until the end of the turn. (Inquisitor)
Restored Aim – Generates aim if the Inquisitor has been healed since his last turn. (Inquisitor)
Trial Accuracy – Enhances the Inquisitor’s accuracy against the current trial target. (Inquisitor)
Judgment Call – The Inquisitor’s next attack deals additional light damage enhanced by current aim. (Inquisitor)
Restoration Screen – Ameliorates afflictions on the Inquisitor and generates aim. Must be used as the final action of the turn. (Inquisitor)

Trial of Destruction – Prepared ability that reserves mana. Enhances all ally damage for as long as the trial is maintained. Ends if the Inquisitor attacks a different enemy or is disrupted. (Inquisitor)

Trial of Health – Prepared ability that reserves mana. Heals all allies at the beginning of each of the Inquisitor’s turns for as long as the trial is maintained. Ends if the Inquisitor attacks a different enemy or is disrupted. (Inquisitor)

Trial of Protection – Prepared ability that reserves mana. Enhances all ally defense for as long as the trial is maintained. Ends if the Inquisitor attacks a different enemy or is disrupted. (Inquisitor)
Corruption Punisher – Ranged attack that deals additional damage based on the amount of corruption currently on the target. (Inquisitor)
Decimation Vow – Prepared ranged attack with decimation. Locks its target at time of preparation. Held until fired. (Inquisitor)
Disenchantment Vow – Prepared ranged ability that locks its target at time of preparation. On use, disenchants the target. (Inquisitor)
Divine Inquisition – Makes a number of random ranged attacks based on current divinity, each of which disenchants its target. Consumes all divinity. (Inquisitor)
Divine Justice – Ranged attack with justice and the pinpoint modifier. Consumes all divinity; both effects are enhanced by the total divinity spent. (Inquisitor)
Illumination Judgment – Ranged attack against an illuminated target. Generates additional aim on hit. (Inquisitor)
Justice Aim – Ranged attack with justice. Consumes aim; the justice effect is enhanced by aim spent. (Inquisitor)
Justice Vow – Prepared ranged attack with justice. Locks its target at time of preparation. Held until fired. (Inquisitor)
Phasing Light Shot – Ranged light attack with phasing. (Inquisitor)
Torchwood Shot – Ranged fire attack that illuminates the target. (Inquisitor)
Torment Snipe – Ranged attack that applies affliction power weakness to the target on a critical hit. (Inquisitor)

Trial of Divinity – Prepared ability that reserves mana. At the beginning of each of the Inquisitor’s turns, deals light damage to the trial target based on current divinity. Ends if the Inquisitor attacks a different enemy or is disrupted. (Inquisitor)

Trial of Justice – Prepared ability that reserves mana. Enhances the Inquisitor’s damage against the trial target based on current aim and justice value. Ends if the Inquisitor attacks a different enemy or is disrupted. (Inquisitor)

Trial of Purity – Prepared ability that reserves mana. Enhances all ally affliction resistance for as long as the trial is maintained. Ends if the Inquisitor attacks a different enemy or is disrupted. (Inquisitor)

r.t: — The Fighter's foundational resource, growing steadily with each tick over the course of battle and capping at 100. Many abilities require a prerequisite expertise level without consuming it — a threshold to cross rather than a cost to pay — while others spend expertise outright for a stronger effect. A Fighter who tracks her floor carefully, knowing which abilities merely require expertise and which actually draw it down, keeps access to a continuous stream of options through a long fight rather than being forced to choose between patience and power.

— Minor-action postures that remain active from initiation until switched. Switching stances never resets accumulated expertise, letting a Fighter shift tactics mid-battle without losing what she's built. Every stance carries an Initial Stance class skill, letting her begin battle already in that stance — even one she hasn't equipped as an ability — without spending an action, and an Advanced Stance class skill that upgrades the stance's core effect once purchased.

— A suite of buffs whose strength scales with the Fighter's current expertise level, applied to a single ally for a duration of roughly three rounds. Refreshing an existing Training updates it to the Fighter's current expertise if that value has since climbed higher than when it was first applied, rewarding a Fighter who checks back in on her buffs as her expertise grows over the course of a fight.

— Reactive abilities that reserve a portion of expertise up front rather than spending it immediately, holding that reservation in wait for a specific trigger. If the trigger fires, the reserved expertise is spent to retroactively upgrade the outcome of the triggering action — turning a miss into a hit, a hit into a critical, a glancing blow into a regular one, or guaranteeing a parry against an incoming attack. If the trigger never comes, the reservation lapses unused. This makes Stratagems a bet on anticipation rather than a straightforward expenditure, distinct from the simple threshold-gated abilities that require expertise without ever touching a reaction.

— The Fighter's relationship with her equipment, expressed both mechanically and thematically. A dedicated Slot Passive category rewards investment in a specific weapon type — axe, hammer, sword, and beyond — with its own bonuses independent of expertise level entirely. This mechanical layer sits alongside a thematic one: subclasses are built around meaningfully different equipment philosophies, from the raw power of large two-handed weapons, to the speed and volume of dual-wielding, to the balanced defense of sword-and-board, giving weapon choice real identity weight rather than treating it as a cosmetic flourish.

si.t: Corporeal Punishment – Deals damage to an enemy in response to an ally dying. (Judge)
Doom Punishment – Lowers the damage and defense of an enemy in response to an ally dying. (Judge)
Follow Judgment Threshold – Threshold ability. Possesses a target ally. (Judge)
Punishment Guard – The Judge gains enhanced damage whenever her guarded ally is attacked. (Judge)
Spiritual Punishment – Disenchants a target enemy and causes mana loss in response to an ally dying. (Judge)
Aspect of Force – Any enemy that attacks the target unit is delayed. (Judge)
Delegated Punishment – Commands an ally to attack the enemy that killed an ally on the previous turn. (Judge)
Influence Provocation – Compels all enemies over which the Judge has influence to attack her. (Judge)
Just Punishment – Melee attack with justice against the enemy that killed an ally on the previous turn. (Judge)
Mind Over Matter – Enhances the Judge’s defense against the next attack. Any damage reduced by this defense is converted into a damage shield. (Judge)
Pain is an Illusion – The next instance of damage dealt to a target ally is converted to illusory damage instead. (Judge)
Possessive Protection – Possesses a target enemy that attacks the guarded ally, forcing it to act against its own side. (Judge)
Reparation Punishment – Possesses the enemy that killed an ally on the previous turn and forces it to attack another enemy. (Judge)
Sleep Threshold – Incapacitates a single target. Requires threshold. (Judge)
Brilliant Blow – Light elemental melee attack that afflicts the target with a light hex and grants the Judge light retaliation. (Judge)
Face My Fears – Transfers all illusory damage currently on the Judge to all enemies over which she has influence. (Judge)
Fire Hammer – Fire melee attack with increased damage against compelled enemies. (Judge)
Hammer of Vengeance – Melee attack with justice, usable only following being attacked by the target since last turn. (Judge)
Hold in Contempt – Physical magic attack against a single target that incapacitates it. (Judge)

Judgment Partnership – Prepared melee attack reaction that fires after an ally dies, with the guarded ally making a simultaneous attack. If the ally who dies is the guarded ally, the attack is a guaranteed critical. (Judge)
Justice Blast – Magic attack against all enemies with damage increased based on current influence and justice value. (Judge)
Justice Influence – Magic attack that deals damage and generates influence over all enemies based on current justice value. (Judge)
Mana Burn Strike – Melee attack that causes mana burn on the target. (Judge)
Mount Giant Owl – Summons a giant owl as a mount companion. (Judge)
Ultimate Punishment – Magic attack against all enemies, usable only on the turn after an enemy dies. (Judge)
Animate Totem – Commands the current totem companion to make an attack against a target enemy. (Totemist)
Deeply Etched – The Totemist’s next rune proc does not consume a use from the rune. (Totemist)
Restore from the Earth – Heals the current companion and delays it. (Totemist)

Runic Rage – While this wrath is active, the Totemist does not lose uses from runes and has an increased chance to proc them. When this wrath ends, all runes are lost and the Totemist becomes cursed. (Totemist)
Totem Lure – The current totem companion provokes all enemies. (Totemist)
Totem Shield – Consumes anguish to grant the current companion a damage shield. (Totemist)
Rage of the Totem – Generates anguish based on the total damage the current totem companion has taken. (Totemist)
Totem Link – Establishes a pain link and heal siphon between the Totemist and the companion until the Totemist’s next turn. (Totemist)
Totem of Lightning – Summons a totem companion that deals air damage to a random enemy whenever any enemy uses a magic attack. (Totemist)
Totem of Protection – Summons a totem companion that grants a damage shield to all allies on each of its turns. (Totemist)
Totem of Speed – Summons a totem companion that quickens a random ally on each of its turns. (Totemist)
Totem of Temptation – Summons a totem companion that taunts a random enemy on each of its turns. (Totemist)
Totem of the Elements – Summons a totem companion that enhances the elemental resistance and elemental power of all allies. (Totemist)
Apex Mountain – Melee attack that costs mana with clobbering and a chance to proc maximum damage. (Totemist)
Battle Totem – Creates a totem companion that makes a melee attack each turn and enhances the Totemist’s melee damage while active. (Totemist)
Call to the Mountains – Earth melee attack against a single target with a chance to proc earth damage against all enemies. (Totemist)
Monolith Bash – Earth melee attack with increased maximum damage. (Totemist)
Mudslide – Earth magic attack against an enemy with earth vulnerability that also deals earth damage to all enemies. (Totemist)
Rage Totem – Creates a totem companion based on current anguish. The totem’s damage increases with the Totemist’s anguish. (Totemist)
Runic Totem – Creates a totem companion constructed from a primed defense rune, a primed damage rune, and a primed power rune. (Totemist)
Stone Blade – Melee attack that procs earth empowerment on the Totemist. (Totemist)
Stone Spirits – Earth magic storm attack. Can be sustained at reduced cost to repeat. (Totemist)
Totemic Bash – Melee attack with clobbering that also strikes two random additional enemies with clobbering. (Totemist)
Totem Wall – Summons a duplicate of the current totem companion for every ally. (Totemist)
Vampire Bat Rune – Element rune. Untyped magic attack against a single target with life drain. (Totemist)
Midnight Blood – Afflicts the target with dark vulnerability and dark bleed simultaneously. (Vivisectionist)
Planned Restoration – The Vivisectionist heals at the beginning of his next turn. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Advantage – Generates advantage following a ruthless attack. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Counter – The Vivisectionist’s counters can deal ruthless damage until his next turn. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Shadow – The Vivisectionist gains hidden following a ruthless attack. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Soul – Spirit buff. Lowers the damage threshold required to trigger ruthless damage. Consumes additional spirit power whenever ruthless damage is dealt. (Vivisectionist)
Blood Snare – Afflicts a bleeding enemy with speed weakness. (Vivisectionist)
Bloody Advantage – Spends health to gain advantage. Backbiting. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Blood – Following a ruthless attack against an enemy, deals a bleed based on the ruthless damage dealt. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Night – Following a ruthless attack, the Vivisectionist gains a dark damage add. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Poison – Grants the Vivisectionist a poison that deals additional damage and ruthless damage. (Vivisectionist)
Seeping Counters – The Vivisectionist’s counters before his next turn deal additional bleed damage. (Vivisectionist)
Blood Fountain – Afflicts the target with an untyped bleed and deals ranged damage to all other enemies. (Vivisectionist)
Bloodwrack – Ranged attack against a bleeding target with enhanced damage based on the number of bleeds currently on it. (Vivisectionist)
Bloody Pain – Melee attack that causes bleed and stuns the target. (Vivisectionist)
Dual Dark Toxic Strike – Ranged attack that causes both untyped and dark bleed and applies venomous. Consumes advantage. (Vivisectionist)
Maximum Pain – Melee attack with a chance to proc maximum damage. (Vivisectionist)
Midnight Critical – Ranged attack that afflicts the target with dark vulnerability on a critical hit. (Vivisectionist)
Plague Rancor – Melee attack against a target suffering from contagion. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Backstab – Melee attack against a hidden enemy. Consumes advantage to deal ruthless damage. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Stun – Melee attack with ruthless. On kill, stuns all remaining enemies. (Vivisectionist)
Ruthless Wave – Ruthless dark magic attack against all enemies. (Vivisectionist)
Spirit Darkness – Dark magic attack against all enemies. The Vivisectionist gains hidden. Consumes spirit power. (Vivisectionist)
Spirit Poison Shot – Ranged attack with venomous. Consumes spirit power. (Vivisectionist)
Weeping Darkness – Piercing dark bleed against all enemies. (Vivisectionist)
Detonation Counter – The next counter detonates all conditions on the target. If the target has no detonations present, it adds one. (Drifter)
Elusion Concoction – Consumes ammo to grant an ally dodge enhancement and hidden. (Drifter)
Focused Mana – Gain mana if focused. (Drifter)
Mindful Focus – Gain focus if in Third Eye form and move to Heart form. (Drifter)
Move Like Smoke – Expend focus when next attacked to become intangible against that attack. (Drifter)
Tranquil Dodge – Gain focus if the Drifter dodged since last turn. (Drifter)
Chakra Counters – Consume all chakras to cause the next several counters to hit twice. (Drifter)
Counter Fire – Expends focus to guarantee the next attack is countered. (Drifter)
Dragon Static – Grants air retaliation that increases over time and resets each time it activates. Requires dragon form. (Drifter)
Focus Infusion – Infusion that can be detonated to apply focus. (Drifter)
Focused Recovery – Sacrifice focus to heal an ally. (Drifter)
Teknos Counter – Counter the next ranged attack, consuming ammo and with effect based on ammo type. (Drifter)
Third Eye Focus – Illuminates target enemy and focuses the Drifter. Requires Third Eye form and moves to Heart form. (Drifter)
Waters of Focus – Focuses the entire team. Consumes water ammo. (Drifter)

Crane Feathers – Melee attack requiring crane form that grants enchantments based on open chakras: focus, haste, intangible, enhanced counter, enhanced dodge, air empowered, and air shielded. Sets form to monkey on hit and lowers form on miss. (Drifter)
Critical Shot – Ranged attack that expends focus to increase critical chance and critical damage. (Drifter)
Disarm Gun – Ranged attack requiring focus that consumes focus and disarms on critical. (Drifter)
Focus Shot – Ranged attack that requires focus, with increased accuracy and critical chance. (Drifter)
Focusing Discharge – Ranged attack that grants focus on critical strike. (Drifter)
Gun Kata – Consume all ammo to make that number of random ranged attacks. (Drifter)
Interminable Focus – Melee attack requiring focus with amplification. Amplification ends when focus is lost. (Drifter)
Lucky Focus Shot – Ranged attack with blessed damage. Requires the Drifter to be focused. (Drifter)
Ricochet Focus – Ranged attack that expends focus to strike a second random target. (Drifter)
Snake Fist – Unerring melee attack that requires snake form and raises form on use. Enhances accuracy. (Drifter)
Static Spire – Summons a companion that lasts for a duration based on ammunition used and grants retaliation effects to allies. (Drifter)
Affliction Guard – Grants the guarded target enhanced affliction resistance. (Exemplar)
Disregard Corruption – The next blocked attack deals no corrupt damage. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Critical – Guarantee a critical with the next attack following the guarded ally suffering a critical. (Exemplar)
Forcefield Block – Restore a damage shield based on damage taken after blocking. Requires an active damage shield. (Exemplar)
Perfect Shielding – Lose elemental shielded to gain immunity to that element until the Exemplar's next turn. (Exemplar)
Prevent Corruption – Convert the next corrupt damage from the target before the Exemplar's next turn to normal damage. (Exemplar)
Adaptive Shielding – Threshold ability that grants elemental shielding to the Exemplar based on the last element to deal damage. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Counterblow – Counter the next melee attack from the target before the Exemplar's next turn. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Counterspell – Counterspell the next magic attack from the target before the Exemplar's next turn. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Resistance – Purge the team of the next affliction that the Exemplar resists. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Shield – Block the next attack made by the target. (Exemplar)
Imbue with Justice – Grant the target a justice proc. (Exemplar)
Light Shielding – Threshold ability that grants light shielded to the Exemplar. (Exemplar)
Return Arrows – Reflect the next ranged attack from the target before the Exemplar's next turn. (Exemplar)
All or Nothing Example – Melee attack with lower accuracy that deals maximized damage on hit. (Exemplar)
Blocking Charge – Follows blocking an attack with a mounted melee attack versus a column. (Exemplar)
Essence Breaker – Melee attack that lowers the target's elemental power. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Challenge – Initial Effect: Taunt all enemies and gain enhanced defense. Basic Effect: Attack and provoke. Challenge Effect: Attack, taunt challenge, and pain link. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Guard – Reflects the next damage dealt to the targeted unit back to the challenged target. (Exemplar)
Exemplary Revenge – Deals damage to the target based on health lost by the guarded ally. (Exemplar)
Forcefield Breaker – Melee attack with a chance to disenchant a damage shield. Costs mana. (Exemplar)
Justice Delay – Melee attack that delays with justice. (Exemplar)
Maximum Response – Melee attack in response to the guarded ally being attacked that deals maximized damage. (Exemplar)
Mount Tiger – Summons a tiger mount. (Exemplar)
Threshold Challenge – Threshold ability that allows the Exemplar to switch challenge targets and then deal massive damage to the new challenge. (Exemplar)
Brutal Throw – Melee attack that requires snake, tiger, or leopard form. Stuns target with a chance to knock them prone. (Pugilist)
Convert to Illusion – Converts the damage of the next ability to illusory. (Illusionist)
Dissuading Figment – Chance to avert all enemies based on illusory damage on them. (Illusionist)
Empowered Illusion – Enhance the damage of the next illusory attack. (Illusionist)
Influence of Illusion – Extends illusory damage based on influence. (Illusionist)
Prepared Disbelief – Prevents illusory damage that would be dealt to the Illusionist before her next turn. (Illusionist)
False Empathy – Prepared ability that deals illusory damage to the next enemy to damage the unit, based on damage dealt. (Illusionist)
Illusory Domination – Possess the target enemy if it is above the illusory damage threshold. (Illusionist)
Illusory Echo – Illusory damage based on the previous damage dealt. (Illusionist)
Illusory Weakness – The target takes more damage from illusions. (Illusionist)
Overwhelm the Senses – Distract and blind the target based on illusory damage present. (Illusionist)
Phantasmal Influence – Generate influence on all enemies based on their current illusory damage. (Illusionist)
Unmitigated Illusion – Causes illusory damage to both allies and enemies. (Illusionist)
Acid Figment – Earth bleed versus a single target using illusory damage. (Illusionist)
Attuned Illusion – Magic attack dealing illusory damage of the attuned element. (Illusionist)
Bright Figment – Illusory light hex that illuminates and blinds on trigger. (Illusionist)
Broken Reality – Deal illusory damage to the target based on current damage on the target. (Illusionist)
Conflux Illusion – Magic attack versus all enemies using every element and dealing illusory damage. Requires at least 5 elements charged. (Illusionist)
False Lightning – Strikes three random targets with illusory air damage, stacking. (Illusionist)
Frost Delusion – Afflicts target with illusory water damage hex. (Illusionist)
Illusion Cantrip – Illusory water damage. Requires both air and water attunement. (Illusionist)
Illusory Blast – Arcane illusory damage versus all enemies. (Illusionist)
Illusory Darkness – Dark element illusory damage and blind versus a single target. (Illusionist)
Illusory Flames – Fire element illusory damage versus all enemies. (Illusionist)
Illusory Heartstrike - Deal illusory damage to the target based on heartstrike value. (Illusionist)
Phantasmal Pain – Deal illusory damage to all enemies based on their current influence. (Illusionist)
Companion Barrier – Grants the companion a barrier. (Invoker)
Companion Forcefield – Grants the companion a damage shield. (Invoker)
Companion Sap – Drain mana from the companion to feed the Invoker at the beginning of each turn. Toggled. (Invoker)

Fire Domain – Grants a fire damage add to all allies. Requires a minimum divinity to activate and consumes divinity each turn. Generates divinity when the Invoker uses fire abilities. Lasts as long as divinity remains above the minimum threshold. (Invoker)
Invert Cross – The next cross ability deals its row effect to the column and its column effect to the row. (Invoker)
Restoring Endowment – The next companion summoned heals itself completely and purges on its first turn. (Invoker)
Eros Heal – Heals an ally. Consumes Eros. (Invoker)
Justice Evolution – Grants the companion's attack a justice proc and reserves mana. (Invoker)
Justice Heal – Heal a target ally based on the Invoker's justice value with the last enemy attacked. (Invoker)
Light Evolution – Provides light damage to the companion's attacks. (Invoker)
Strength of Light – Grants a light damage add to an ally's next attack. Requires Eros. (Invoker)
Taunt Command – The companion taunts all enemies and the Invoker heals it. (Invoker)
Thanatos Purge – Consume Thanatos to purge a target ally. (Invoker)
Companion's Cross – The Invoker deals magic damage versus a column while the companion attacks a row. (Invoker)
Cross of Earth and Sky – Deals earth damage versus a row and air damage versus a column. (Invoker)
Cross of Eros and Thanatos – Deals damage to a row enhanced by Thanatos and damage to a column enhanced by Eros. (Invoker)
Cross of Fire and Frost – Deals fire damage versus a row and water damage versus a column. (Invoker)
Cross of Sun and Shadow – Deals dark damage versus a row and light damage versus a column. (Invoker)
Divine Ally – Consumes all divinity to summon a companion. Power is based on divinity used to summon and current divinity. (Invoker)
Divine Cross – Deals light damage to a row and column, delays the column and lowers damage versus the row. (Invoker)
Extreme Illumination – Magic light attack versus all enemies that causes illuminated. (Invoker)
Irradiating Light – Magic light attack versus all illuminated enemies. (Invoker)
Justice Command – The companion makes an attack benefiting from justice. (Invoker)
Partnered Healing – Heal all allies with a heal enhanced by the companion's healing power. (Invoker)
Summoned Invocation – The companion begins to cast a powerful light magic attack versus all enemies. (Invoker)
Acid Vial Rune – Element rune. Magic earth attack versus a single target with earth bleed. (Lore Keeper)
Caustic Rain – Earth damage and decimate versus all enemies. (Lore Keeper)
Dark Emergence – Dark magic attack that afflicts the target with dark vulnerability. (Lore Keeper)
Dim Malediction – Dark magic attack versus a maledicted target that grants intangible. (Lore Keeper)
Distillation of Darkness – Dark magic attack versus all enemies and grants the Lore Keeper a dark damage add based on targets hit. (Lore Keeper)
Distillation of Earth – Earth magic attack versus all enemies and grants the Lore Keeper an earth damage add based on targets hit. (Lore Keeper)
Drought Field – Tire and earth hex on all enemies. (Lore Keeper)
Forbid Attack – Causes the target to damage all allies whenever it attacks. (Lore Keeper)
Forbid Magic – Causes the target to take earth damage whenever it casts a spell. (Lore Keeper)
Mass Earth Vulnerability – Afflict all enemies with earth vulnerability. (Lore Keeper)
Midnight Mind – Dark magic attack versus all enemies that also damages mana. (Lore Keeper)
Snuffed Lantern Rune – Element rune. Magic dark damage versus all enemies. (Lore Keeper)
Forbid Counter – Causes the target to attack itself whenever it counterattacks. (Lore Keeper)
Forbid Critical – Causes the target to become disarmed whenever it scores a critical hit. (Lore Keeper)
Forbid Dodge – Causes the target to become prone whenever it dodges an attack. (Lore Keeper)
Ghost Rune – Defense rune. The target becomes intangible when attacked. (Lore Keeper)
Glimpse of Doom – The target enemy cannot dodge the next attack. If not attacked before its turn, its next attack misses. (Lore Keeper)

Rune of Fate – Timing rune. Countdown on the target that deals damage based on its current vulnerability value on trigger. Recharges while mana allows. Can be consumed for its expiration effect. (Lore Keeper)
Stone Vulnerability – Afflict a target enemy with earth vulnerability. (Lore Keeper)
Brief Curse – Prevent the target from activating procs until end of next turn. Prepared. (Lore Keeper)
Darkeye Rune – Attacks of the target cause blindness. (Lore Keeper)
Enduring Mind – Prevents mana loss from enemies until end of next turn. (Lore Keeper)
Forbid Heal – The next time the target heals an ally, that ally is also maledicted. (Lore Keeper)
Mana Enthusiasm – Gain mana for each enemy that dies during this turn. Alpha. (Lore Keeper)
Momentary Mana – Prepared ability that grants mana that disappears at end of turn. (Lore Keeper)
Explosive Images – Each time a mirror image is lost until the Phantasm's next turn, damage all enemies. Omega. (Phantasm)
Mirror Dodging – Enhance dodge and spell dodge based on total mirror images. (Phantasm)
Mirror Flanking – The Phantasm loses a mirror image and flanks an enemy. (Phantasm)
Mirror Illusion – Consumes one mirror image to deal illusory damage to the target. (Phantasm)
Phantasmal Ground – Spirit aura that causes enemies to have a chance to become flanked at the beginning of their turn. Requires a spirit orb. (Phantasm)
Refresh Reflection – Generates one mirror image. Requires the Phantasm to already have mirror images. (Phantasm)
Enhanced Spirit – Spirit aura that increases current enhancements on all allies and causes them to last as long as this aura has spirit power to consume. (Phantasm)
Ghost Song – Periodically grants intangible to audience members. (Phantasm)
Mirror Curse – Consume a mirror image to cause an arcane hex on the target. (Phantasm)
Phantasmal Bow – Grants the Phantasm illusory damage and avert on attacks. Consumes spirit power. Requires a spirit orb. (Phantasm)
Phantasmal Restoration – Spirit aura that heals all allies at the beginning of the Phantasm's turn. Requires a spirit orb. (Phantasm)
Phantasmal Thorns – Grants the Phantasm illusory retaliation. Consumes spirit power. Requires a spirit orb. (Phantasm)
Reflections of Self – Creates multiple mirror images. (Phantasm)
Animated Reflection – Summons a companion with power based on mirror images. (Phantasm)
Eldritch Singularity – Control ability that disrupts, disenchants, and causes mana loss for all enemies. (Phantasm)
Hall of Mirrors – Magic arcane attack versus all enemies dealing illusory damage enhanced by mirror images. (Phantasm)
Hallucination Note – Ranged attack that deals illusory damage and adds the target to the audience. (Phantasm)
Mirror Onslaught – Consumes all mirror images to make that number of random melee attacks. (Phantasm)
Mirror Shot – Distant ranged attack that generates one mirror image. (Phantasm)
Mirror Spell – Arcane magic attack that flanks the target and consumes a mirror image. (Phantasm)
Mirror Strike – Melee attack against a flanked enemy. Requires a mirror image. (Phantasm)
Mosquito Note – Ranged attack that drains life and adds the target to the audience. (Phantasm)
Penetrating Refrain – Ranged attack that damages each enemy in the audience with penetrate, causing untyped bleed and refreshing the song. (Phantasm)
Reflecting Strike – Two melee attacks against the target and generate a mirror image. Requires a mirror image. (Phantasm)
Sleep Note – Incapacitate a target enemy and add it to the audience. (Phantasm)
Aggravating Speed – Quicken the Reaver based on aggravation and reduce accuracy of the next attack. Aggravating. Consumes rage. (Reaver)

Aggravating Stance – Gains expertise whenever the Reaver misses. All attacks gain aggravating, causing increased damage and reduced accuracy for each successive hit, resetting when the Reaver misses. (Reaver)
Critical Aggravation – Increase aggravation value then enhance critical damage based on aggravation. (Reaver)
Critical Reaving – Aggravation applies to critical chance and critical damage instead of accuracy and damage. Toggled. Cannot lower critical chance below minimum value. (Reaver)
Move Past Aggravation – Lower aggravation value to 0. Enhance accuracy of the next attack based on former aggravation value. (Reaver)
Reaving Expertise – Spot an endangered enemy and gain expertise. (Reaver)
Reaving Rage – Spot an endangered enemy to gain rage. (Reaver)
Aggravating Rage – Enhance damage and reduce accuracy of the next attack. Aggravating. Consumes rage. (Reaver)
Aggravating Tenacity – Raises aggravation value based on damage taken before next turn. (Reaver)
Attention Seeker – Follows a critical by compelling all enemies. Can be used while berserk. (Reaver)
Expert Criticals – Enhances the critical damage of the target, increased by expertise. (Reaver)
Reaping Aggravation – The next attack with aggravation that misses still deals damage based on aggravation. (Reaver)
Spread Aggravation – Enhance the damage of allies based on aggravation value. (Reaver)
Aggravating Penance – Melee attack with aggravating and backbiting. (Reaver)
Aggravating Shatter – Melee attack with aggravating and shattering. (Reaver)
Aggravating Slam – Melee attack with aggravating and stun. (Reaver)
Aggravating Slash – Melee attack with aggravating. (Reaver)
